description: A clinical swallowing examination using six identifiers (dysphonia, dysarthria, abnormal gag reflex, abnormal volitional cough, cough after swallow, and voice change after swallow) can reliably predict aspiration risk in acute stroke patients
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as a 'systematic replication study' with 'minimal variations in design' of Daniels et al. (1997), using the same six clinical identifiers of aspiration risk with FEES as the criterion standard. The results confirmed the original study's finding that clinical examination underestimates aspiration risk, with the replication's sensitivity (86%) and poor specificity (30%) being consistent with and supporting the original study's conclusions about the limitations of clinical swallowing examination.

original_authors: Rosenbek, J.C.; Robbins, J.A.; Roecker, E.B.; Coyle, J.L.; Wood, J.L.
original_title: A penetration-aspiration scale
description: The Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS) achieves adequate interjudge and intrajudge reliability when used to assess swallowing via videofluoroscopy (VFSS) in dysphagic patients
explanation: The authors explicitly describe their study as 'a replication of a study using videofluoroscopy (VFSS)' and conclude: 'The findings of this study support and enhance the findings of Rosenbek et al. Both intrajudge and interjudge reliabilities were high in this study; as a matter of fact, they were higher than those reported by Rosenbek et al.' The study successfully replicated PAS reliability using FEES instead of VFSS.

original_authors: Leder, S.; Ross, D.
original_title: Investigation of the causal relationship between tracheotomy and aspiration in the acute care setting
description: There is no causal relationship between tracheotomy and aspiration status in hospitalized patients, as measured by pre- and post-tracheotomy fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES)
explanation: The paper is explicitly titled 'A Direct Replication Study' and concludes: 'This direct replication study confirmed previous findings [8], i.e., there is no causal relationship between tracheotomy and the presence of a tracheotomy tube and aspiration status.' Results from the replication (N=25) were entirely consistent with the original study (N=20).

original_authors: Leder, S.; Ross, D.
original_title: Incidence of vocal fold immobility in patients with dysphagia
description: Vocal fold immobility (VFI) is present in approximately 5.6% of patients referred for dysphagia evaluation and, when present, confers approximately twice the odds of aspiration compared to patients without VFI in the same referred population
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the conclusion: 'There were no inconsistent results noted among the original, direct replication, and combined data sets,' and the Discussion confirms 'Both the incidence of VFI (right, left, or bilateral) and the incidence of aspiration were confirmed.' The replication found consistent results across all key outcome measures.

original_authors: Suiter, D.; Leder, S.
original_title: Clinical utility of the 3 ounce water swallow test
description: A 3-ounce water swallow challenge (using FEES as reference standard, single nonblinded rater) has 96.5% sensitivity and 97.9% negative predictive value for predicting aspiration risk in hospitalized patients across diverse diagnoses
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as a 'systematic replication study' and conclude: 'This systematic replication study has verified our previous research findings by using videofluoroscopy in a small population of male patients.' The replication confirmed key findings (100% sensitivity, 100% NPV) using a different reference standard (VFSS instead of FEES) and multiple blinded raters instead of a single nonblinded rater.

original_authors: Agueda, L.; Velazquez-Cruz, R.; Urreizti, R.; Yoskovitz, G.; Sarrion, P.; Jurado, S.; Guerri, R.; Garcia-Giralt, N.; Nogues, X.; Mellibovsky, L.; Diez-Perez, A.; Marie, P.; Balcells, S.; Grinberg, D.
original_title: Functional relevance of the BMD-associated polymorphism rs312009: novel involvement of RUNX2 in LRP5 transcriptional regulation
description: The rs312009 SNP in the LRP5 gene (located at a RUNX2 transcription factor binding site) is functionally associated with bone mineral density, with the C allele associated with lower BMD
explanation: The replication found a strong statistically significant association of rs312009 in the LRP5 gene with lumbar spine BMD (P < 0.0083 after Bonferroni correction), with CC genotype women showing the worst bone parameters and 2.82 times increased osteoporosis risk. The authors state: 'This is consistent with previous work in our country, whereby postmenopausal women with the TT genotype showed higher LS-BMD than did women with the TC/CC genotype.'

original_authors: Vidal, C.; Formosa, R.; Xuereb-Anastasi, A.
original_title: Functional polymorphisms within the TNFRSF11B (osteoprotegerin) gene increase the risk for low bone mineral density
description: The rs4876869 SNP in the TNFRSF11B (osteoprotegerin) gene, which affects pre-mRNA splicing in vitro, is associated with low bone mineral density as part of a haplotype with other SNPs
explanation: The replication found no statistically significant association between rs4876869 and BMD at any skeletal site. Table 3 shows FN-sBMD P = 0.090 and LS-sBMD P = 0.504 (unadjusted), both non-significant after Bonferroni correction (threshold P < 0.0083). Table 4 (covariate-adjusted) shows FN-sBMD P = 0.178. Table 5 shows non-significant osteoporosis risk: FN adjusted OR = 1.67 (95% CI 0.77-3.62, P = 0.192), LS adjusted OR = 1.36 (95% CI 0.88-2.10, P = 0.170). The original paper (Vidal et al.) found rs4876869 significant only within a haplotype (P = 0.01), not independently. The authors note this negative result 'is in agreement with previous results in which no association was detected between this SNP and BMD when analyzed independently.' Classified as failure because the replication paper's stated aim was to test this functional polymorphism's association with BMD and no significant association was found.

original_authors: Hoppman, N.; Mclenithan, J.; Mcbride, D.; Shen, H.; Bruder, J.; Bauer, R.; Shaffer, J.; Liu, J.; Streeten, E.; Shuldiner, A.; Kammerer, C.; Mitchell, B.
original_title: A common variant in fibroblast growth factor binding protein 1 (FGFBP1) is associated with bone mineral density and influences gene expression in vitro
description: The rs12503796 SNP in the FGFBP1 gene (located at the promoter region, modulating FGFBP1 expression) is associated with bone mineral density, with an effect that is sex-stratified (only in men)
explanation: The replication found no association between rs12503796 in the FGFBP1 gene and any bone phenotype. Table 3 shows completely non-significant P values: FN-sBMD P = 0.416 (recessive model), LS-sBMD P = 0.427 (dominant model). The SNP was dropped from further adjusted analysis due to its lack of association. The authors note: 'Although Hoppman et al. [17] describe weak associations of this polymorphism with several bone phenotypes in a Mexican-American discovery population and in an Amish replication population, they also report that the association is sex-stratified, so it is associated only with men, not with women. This agrees with the results we have provided in the present paper.' Classified as failure because the paper explicitly aimed to replicate this BMD association and found none in their women-only cohort, even though the null result is expected given the original study's sex-stratified finding (men only).

original_authors: Happé, F.
original_title: An advanced test of theory of mind: understanding of story characters' thoughts and feelings by able autistic, mentally handicapped and normal children and adults
original_journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
description: Children and adolescents with autism/Asperger syndrome show impaired ability to infer mental states (theory of mind) in story contexts using the Strange Stories test, providing context-inappropriate rather than context-appropriate mental state explanations
explanation: The authors explicitly state that 'the results on the mentalistic task were largely consistent with the finding of Happé [15] and Jolliffe and Baron-Cohen [20],' and the paper is subtitled 'A replication study of children and adolescents with Asperger syndrome.' The AS group performed significantly worse than controls on mental state justifications (p < 0.0001), replicating the original finding.

original_authors: Dhaenens, C.; Burnouf, S.; Simonin, C.; Brussel, V.; Duhamel, E.; Defebvre, A.; Duru, L.; Vuillaume, C.; Cazeneuve, I.; Charles, P.; Debruxelles, M.; Verny, C.; Gervais, H.; Azulay, J.P.; Tranchant, C.; Bachoud-Levi, A.C.; Dürr, A.; Buée, L.; Krystkowiak, P.; Sablonnière, B.; Blum, D.; Huntington French Speaking Network
original_title: A genetic variation in the ADORA2A gene modifies age at onset in Huntington's disease
description: A synonymous exchange (Tyr361Tyr) in exon 3 of ADORA2A (rs5751876) significantly modifies the variability in age at onset (earliest AO) of Huntington's disease
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'replicated the previously reported association between the original ADORA2A polymorphism when using the earliest AO' (R2 increased from 0.671 to 0.674, p=0.032), consistent with the original study which also used earliest AO as the outcome measure.

original_authors: Metzger, S.; Rong, J.; Nguyen, H.; Cape, A.; Tomiuk, J.; Soehn, A.; Propping, P.; Freudenberg-Hua, Y.; Freudenberg, J.; Tong, L.; Li, S.; Li, X.; Riess, O.
original_title: Huntingtin-associated protein-1 is a modifier of the age-at-onset of Huntington's disease
description: HAP1 Thr441Met (rs4523977) variation leads to delayed onset of initial symptoms of Huntington's disease, with rare HAP1 Met variant showing stronger interaction with mutated huntingtin and reduced neurodegeneration
explanation: The authors found 'modest evidence for association with the same risk allele as in the original sample' for motor AO (p=0.041), but the association did not replicate for earliest AO, and the CAG-length stratification effect reported by the original did not replicate at all (all p>0.1), leaving an overall picture of partial and limited support.

original_authors: Coppedè, F.; Migheli, F.; Ceravolo, R.; Bregant, E.; Rocchi, A.; Petrozzi, L.; Unti, E.; Lonigro, R.; Siciliano, G.; Migliore, L.
original_title: The hOGG1 Ser326Cys polymorphism and Huntington's disease
description: The OGG1 Ser326Cys (rs1052133) Cys allele is associated with an earlier age at onset and a significantly increased number of CAG repeats in Huntington's disease patients
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'we did not replicate this association,' finding that carriers of at least one Cys allele had almost identical average AO and CAG repeat length compared with Ser/Ser homozygotes, and the genotype explained no additional variance in AO.

original_authors: Yau, M.; Yerges-Armstrong, L.; Liu, Y.; Lewis, C.; Duggan, D.; Renner, J.; Torner, J.; Felson, D.; Mcculloch, C.; Kwoh, C.; Nevitt, M.; Hochberg, M.; Mitchell, B.; Jordan, J.; Jackson, R.
original_title: Genome-wide association study of radiographic knee osteoarthritis in north American Caucasians
description: Variant rs4867568 near LSP1P3 is associated with reduced risk of knee osteoarthritis in North American Caucasians (minor allele T protective, OR = 0.84)
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'we successfully replicated the association of the novel variant rs4867568 with the susceptibility of KOA in a cohort of patients from the Chinese Han population.' The minor allele T of rs4867568 was significantly less frequent in KOA patients than controls (31.5% vs. 36.0%, p = 0.01, OR = 0.82), consistent with a protective role as found in the original Caucasian GWAS.

original_authors: Yau, M.; Yerges-Armstrong, L.; Liu, Y.; Lewis, C.; Duggan, D.; Renner, J.; Torner, J.; Felson, D.; Mcculloch, C.; Kwoh, C.; Nevitt, M.; Hochberg, M.; Mitchell, B.; Jordan, J.; Jackson, R.
original_title: Genome-wide association study of radiographic knee osteoarthritis in north American Caucasians
description: Variant rs143383 in GDF5 is associated with reduced risk of knee osteoarthritis (minor allele C protective) in North American Caucasians
explanation: The authors explicitly state that 'Another successfully replicated SNP was rs143383 in GDF5,' with the minor allele C associated with decreased KOA risk in the Chinese population (24.6% vs. 28.7%, p = 0.02, OR = 0.81 [0.68-0.97]), consistent with the original finding.

original_authors: Yau, M.; Yerges-Armstrong, L.; Liu, Y.; Lewis, C.; Duggan, D.; Renner, J.; Torner, J.; Felson, D.; Mcculloch, C.; Kwoh, C.; Nevitt, M.; Hochberg, M.; Mitchell, B.; Jordan, J.; Jackson, R.
original_title: Genome-wide association study of radiographic knee osteoarthritis in north American Caucasians
description: Variant rs1558902 in FTO is associated with knee osteoarthritis risk in North American Caucasians
explanation: No significant difference in rs1558902 allele or genotype frequencies was found between KOA patients and controls in the Chinese population (p = 0.78, OR = 1.02 [0.88-1.19]). The authors note that 'the lack of association between FTO and KOA has been previously reported in Chinese population,' implying the failure to replicate in this ethnic context is consistent with known genetic heterogeneity.

original_authors: Briellmann, R.; Torn-Broers, Y.; Busuttil, B.
original_title: APOE epsilon4 genotype is associated with an earlier onset of chronic temporal lobe epilepsy
description: The presence of ApoE ε4 allele is associated with an earlier age at onset of temporal lobe epilepsy
explanation: The present study confirmed a significant association between early age at onset of epilepsy and the presence of allele ε4 (ε4+: 10.54±6.36 years vs. ε4−: 16.51±9.90 years; p=0.003), consistent with the original finding (p=0.005). The authors state this is 'the second one that reports an early age at onset in ε4 TLE carriers.'

original_authors: Kanemoto, K.; Kawasaki, J.; Miyamoto, T.
original_title: Interleukin (IL)1beta, IL-1alpha, and IL-1 receptor antagonist gene polymorphisms in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy
description: The IL-1β-511 2-2 genotype is found at a statistically higher frequency in TLE patients with hippocampal sclerosis (TLE-HS+) compared to control subjects
explanation: The present study found no significant difference in IL-1β-511 allele or genotype frequencies between TLE-HS+ patients and controls, contrary to Kanemoto et al.'s positive finding. The authors state 'this association was not observed in five other ethnically variable populations or in our cohort of patients.'

original_authors: Stogmann, E.; Zimprich, A.; Baumgartner, C.
original_title: A functional polymorphism in the prodynorphin gene promotor is associated with temporal lobe epilepsy
description: The PDYN promoter L allele confers an increased risk for temporal lobe epilepsy in patients with a family history of seizures
explanation: The present study found only a non-significant trend of excess L allele in familial TLE patients (OR=1.60, CI 0.82-3.31, p=0.163), compared to the original significant finding (OR=2.25, CI 1.41-3.62, p=0.0006). The authors explicitly state they 'failed to confirm the involvement of... PDYN.'

original_authors: Sandholm, N.; Salem, R.; McKnight, A.; Brennan, E.; Forsblom, C.; Isakova, T.
original_title: New susceptibility loci associated with kidney disease in type 1 diabetes
description: The rs7583877 SNP in AFF3 is associated with increased risk of end-stage renal disease (diabetic nephropathy) in European type 1 diabetes patients
explanation: The authors found no significant association of rs7583877 in AFF3 with diabetic nephropathy in Japanese type 2 diabetes patients (p=0.5210, OR=0.96, 95% CI: 0.86-1.08). The authors conclude that 'the association of 3 SNP loci...was not replicated in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.'

original_authors: Sandholm, N.; Salem, R.; McKnight, A.; Brennan, E.; Forsblom, C.; Isakova, T.
original_title: New susceptibility loci associated with kidney disease in type 1 diabetes
description: The rs12437854 SNP in the RGMA-MCTP2 locus is associated with increased risk of end-stage renal disease (diabetic nephropathy) in European type 1 diabetes patients
explanation: The authors found no significant association of rs12437854 in the RGMA-MCTP2 locus with diabetic nephropathy in Japanese type 2 diabetes patients (all cases: p=0.8831, OR=1.012; ESRD analysis: p=0.0892, OR=0.85). The authors conclude that 'the association of 3 SNP loci...was not replicated in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.'

original_authors: Sandholm, N.; Salem, R.; McKnight, A.; Brennan, E.; Forsblom, C.; Isakova, T.
original_title: New susceptibility loci associated with kidney disease in type 1 diabetes
description: The rs7588550 SNP in ERBB4 is associated with susceptibility to diabetic nephropathy (all nephropathy cases) in European type 1 diabetes patients, with the G allele having a protective effect
explanation: The study found a statistically significant association of rs7588550 in ERBB4 with diabetic nephropathy in Japanese type 2 diabetes patients, but in the opposite direction to the original (p=0.0126, OR=0.79, 95% CI: 0.65-0.95): 'the G allele of rs7588550, which showed a protective effect in the original report, increased the risk of diabetic nephropathy.' The authors conclude this was 'not replicated' due to the inconsistent effect direction.

original_authors: Laeng, B.; Profeti, I.; Saether, L.
original_title: Invisible expressions evoke core impressions
description: Emotional expressions encoded in low spatial frequencies of hybrid face images (invisible to conscious perception) influence perceived friendliness ratings of unfamiliar faces
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'The Invisible Expression effect was successfully replicated (F(2, 38.18) = 16.24, p < 0.001)'. The replication followed Laeng et al.'s procedure but used different stimuli (Karolinska Directed Emotional Faces database) and tested an Italian population, making it a close extension.

original_authors: Yoshida, M.; Dickey, M.; Sturt, P.
original_title: Predictive processing of syntactic structure: sluicing and ellipsis in real-time sentence processing
description: When a wh-phrase indicates parallelism between an upcoming wh-clause and a preceding clause, the parser predictively constructs the wh-clause (gender mismatch effects at the reflexive occur only in wh-NP conditions, but not when a preposition undermines parallelism in wh-PP conditions), suggesting prediction is a parallelism-driven process
explanation: The present study used the same 24 experimental materials from Yoshida et al. but employed a lexicality maze task (rather than self-paced reading) and 324 participants (rather than 40). The authors report the findings are 'partially inconsistent with Yoshida et al.': gender mismatch effects were found in both wh-NP and wh-PP conditions (no wh-type × gender interaction), contradicting the original's finding that prediction is parallelism-driven (only in wh-NP conditions). However, the core finding of predictive structure building was confirmed and even extended, and garden-path effects (absent in the original) were observed.

original_authors: VanderLaan, D.; Forrester, D.; Petterson, L.; Vasey, P.
original_title: Offspring production among the extended relatives of Samoan men and fa'afafine
description: Female relatives (mothers, grandmothers, aunts) of androphilic Samoan males (fa'afafine) exhibit elevated reproductive output compared to those of gynephilic men, consistent with the sexually antagonistic gene hypothesis
explanation: The replication found that mothers and maternal grandmothers of fa'afafine had significantly elevated reproductive output (consistent with the original), but failed to replicate the paternal grandmother effect found by VanderLaan et al. (2012). The authors concluded support for the SAGH is 'equivocal' because no maternal aunt effect was found, which would represent the 'gold standard' evidence for the hypothesis.

original_authors: Leivers, S.; Rhodes, G.; Simmons, L.
original_title: Sperm competition in humans: Mate guarding behavior negatively correlates with ejaculate quality
description: Men who perform mate retention (mate guarding) behavior less frequently produce higher-quality ejaculates, suggesting that humans deploy mate retention behavior and ejaculate quality investment as compensatory anti-cuckoldry tactics
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'this conceptual replication was not successful because we did not identify statistically significant associations between the deployment of mate retention behavior (overall or along the domains of benefit-provisioning or cost-inflicting) and (most assessments of) ejaculate quality.' The study used a different operationalization of ejaculate quality (4 principal components from 17 parameters) and the MRI-SF instrument, constituting a conceptual rather than direct replication.

original_authors: Baker, R.; Bellis, M.
original_title: Human sperm competition: Ejaculate adjustment by males and the function of masturbation
description: Men produce more sperm in ejaculates when they have spent less time together with their partner since the couple's last copulation, indicating ejaculate adjustment in response to sperm competition risk
explanation: The paper explicitly labels itself a 'conceptual replication' of Baker & Bellis, using additional measures of sperm competition risk and updated technology. The main finding of Baker & Bellis — that time spent apart predicts ejaculate quality — was not replicated: 'time spent together since the couple's last copulation was not associated with any of the several indicators of ejaculate quality in the present study.'

original_authors: Albunian, N.; Fraser, G.; Sudholt, D.
original_title: Causes and effects of fitness landscapes in unit test generation
original_journal: Proceedings of the 2020 Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference
description: Fitness landscapes in unit test generation are dominated by neutral regions (plateaus), with ruggedness and neutrality properties measurably affecting search algorithm effectiveness in covering branches
explanation: The authors explicitly replicate Albunian et al.'s (2020) fitness landscape analysis methodology (same six metrics, same random walk approach, same 1000 steps and 30 runs) but apply it to system-level test generation with EvoMaster rather than unit-level testing with EvoSuite. The Conclusions state: 'Our results confirm the existing results reported in the literature for unit testing, albeit with some differences,' with notable differences in the DBI metric between system-level and unit-level testing.

original_authors: Steinthorsdottir, V.
original_title: Genetic predisposition to hypertension is associated with preeclampsia in European and central Asian women
description: The fetal genotype of FLT1 rs4769612 (C allele) increases the risk of preeclampsia in European and Central Asian women
explanation: The replication found that the fetal genotype of rs4769612 was associated with preeclampsia risk in Iranian women under the recessive model (Table 3, P=0.0048), but the C/C genotype was protective (OR=0.34) rather than risk-increasing as reported in the original. The Discussion confirms: 'Steinthorsdottir et al. reported...the C allele increased the risk of PE,' whereas in the replication 'the fetal C/C genotype lowered the risk of PE.' The same genome (fetal) shows association but with reversed effect direction. The authors acknowledge 'discrepancies with previous studies.' Classified as inconclusive because the fetal association was found but with opposite directionality.

original_authors: Steinthorsdottir, V.
original_title: Genetic predisposition to hypertension is associated with preeclampsia in European and central Asian women
description: The maternal genotype of FTO rs1421085 is associated with preeclampsia risk in European and Central Asian women
explanation: The replication found that the maternal genotype of rs1421085 showed no association with preeclampsia in Iranian women (Table 4: all maternal P-values >0.05), directly contradicting the original finding. The Discussion confirms: 'Steinthorsdottir et al. showed for the first time that rs1421085 is significantly associated with PE risk through the maternal genome.' Instead, the fetal genotype was associated under dominant (OR=1.87, P=0.031) and over-dominant (OR=2.01, P=0.034) models. The specific original claim about maternal genome association was not replicated; association was found only through fetal genome. Classified as inconclusive because the variant-disease association exists but through a different biological mechanism (fetal vs. maternal genome).

original_authors: Steinthorsdottir, V.
original_title: Genetic predisposition to hypertension is associated with preeclampsia in European and central Asian women
description: The maternal genotype of ZNF831 rs259983 is associated with preeclampsia susceptibility in European and Central Asian women
explanation: The replication confirmed that the maternal genotype of rs259983 was associated with preeclampsia under the dominant model in Iranian women (OR=0.63, 95% CI 0.40-0.99, P=0.043), consistent with the original GWAS finding. The authors state this result is 'consistent with' Steinthorsdottir et al.

original_authors: Sáez, B.; Servera, M.; Becker, S.; Burns, G.
original_title: Optimal items for assessing sluggish cognitive tempo in children across mother, father, and teacher ratings
original_journal: Journal of Clinical Child & Adolescent Psychology
description: Cognitive disengagement syndrome (CDS) symptoms show strong internal and structural validity relative to ADHD-inattention symptoms, with invariance of CDS symptom loadings and thresholds across mother and father ratings of the same child, and CDS showing stronger associations than ADHD-IN with anxiety and depression
explanation: The paper's title explicitly frames it as 'Replication of Northern Hemisphere Findings in South America.' The PDF confirms all key findings replicate: (1) CDS symptoms had substantial loadings on CDS factor (mothers M=0.78, fathers M=0.71) with near-zero cross-loadings on ADHD-IN, matching prior studies; (2) 14 of 15 CDS symptoms showed invariance across mother/father ratings, described as 'almost identical' to Sáez et al. [8,9]; (3) CDS factor means did not differ across parents (d=-0.06), matching Sáez et al. (d=0.01); (4) external validity pattern replicated — ADHD-IN stronger with ADHD-HI, CDS stronger with anxiety/depression across all source analyses. The Discussion states results were 'highly consistent with the findings from studies in the five earlier studies.' The one minor deviation (CDS and ADHD-IN similarly associated with academic impairment, whereas prior studies found ADHD-IN stronger) is explicitly noted by the authors but does not undermine the overall successful replication pattern.

original_authors: Skar, G.; Graham, S.; Huebner, A.
original_title: Learning loss during the COVID-19 pandemic and emergency remote instruction first grade students' writing: A natural experiment
description: First-grade Norwegian students who experienced COVID-19 emergency remote instruction scored lower on writing quality, handwriting fluency, and attitude toward writing than a pre-pandemic cohort of first-graders in the same schools
explanation: The authors replicated the same methodology with the same cohort one year later (as second-graders) and found no significant differences between the Before and During COVID-19 cohorts on any of the three writing measures. As stated in the Discussion: 'Contrary to our prediction, we did not find statistically significant differences between the Before COVID-19 cohort and the During COVID-19 cohort on any of the three writing measures: writing quality, handwriting fluency, or attitude toward writing.' The COVID-19 learning loss effect observed in first grade did not persist to second grade.

original_authors: Haq, Fitash Ul; Shin, Donghwan; Briand, Lionel
original_title: Many-objective reinforcement learning for online testing of DNN-enabled systems
original_journal: IEEE/ACM 45th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
description: MORLOT (Many-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Online Testing), which combines RL and many-objective search, outperforms random testing and search-based techniques for online testing of Deep Neural Network-enabled Autonomous Driving Systems in terms of safety requirements violations exposed within a given time budget
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'The replication does not confirm the finding that many-objective Reinforcement Learning, specifically MORLOT, outperforms the random baseline in ADS testing.' They found that when the random baseline is run under the same detection conditions as MORLOT (correcting a confounding factor), MORLOT and random are 'statistically indistinguishable' in both effectiveness and efficiency across all three test routes.

original_authors: Arcuri, A.
original_title: Test suite generation with the Many Independent Objective (MIO) algorithm
description: The LAST configuration of feedbackDirectedSampling is the most effective value for MIO-based test suite generation in EvoMaster, with no single configuration being a clear winner across all case studies
explanation: The replication found no clear winner among the three feedbackDirectedSampling settings, which 'reaffirmed the same conclusions as in the original study' — thus the original finding (that no configuration is clearly dominant) was successfully replicated across a larger set of SUTs and a newer tool version.

original_authors: Arcuri, A.; Galeotti, J.
original_title: Handling SQL databases in automated system test generation
original_journal: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
description: A value of 5 for the maxSQLInitActionsPerMissingData parameter yields the highest average code coverage in EvoMaster when testing REST APIs with SQL-backed databases
explanation: The replication confirmed that the value of 5 for maxSQLInitActionsPerMissingData was the most effective, consistent with the original study: 'We found that a configuration of 5 for maxSQLInitActionsPerMissingData is indeed the most effective' across line coverage, branch coverage, and fault detection metrics.

original_authors: Zhang, M.; Arcuri, A.
original_title: Enhancing resource-based test case generation for RESTful APIs with SQL handling
original_journal: International Symposium on Search Based Software Engineering
description: A value of 0.5 for probOfApplySQLActionToCreateResources is the most effective setting for maximizing code coverage in EvoMaster REST API testing
explanation: The replication confirmed the original finding. Table 10 shows Vargha-Delaney effect sizes comparing 0.5 vs other settings are all near 0.50 (no significant difference favoring alternatives), with 0.5 slightly ahead on average for line and branch coverage (Â=0.51-0.53). The authors explicitly conclude: 'Evaluating the collective data from all 15 REST APIs, we determined that a 0.5 setting consistently provided the best overall performance, aligning with the conclusions of the original study.' While individual SUTs showed variation (e.g., proxy-print and scout-api favored different values), the aggregate finding clearly replicates. Verified against PDF Tables 9-10 and RQ1 findings summary.

original_authors: Zhang, M.; Arcuri, A.
original_title: Adaptive hypermutation for search-based system test generation: a study on REST APIs with EvoMaster
original_journal: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
description: A value of 0.5 for probOfRandomSampling is the optimal setting for balancing exploration and exploitation in EvoMaster's MIO algorithm for REST API testing
explanation: The replication found that 0.8 outperformed the original optimal value of 0.5 for probOfRandomSampling, contradicting the original study. The replication paper summarizes: 'Contrary to the original articles that found 0.5 to be the optimum, here we discovered that 0.8 performed better across multiple case studies' — indicating the original recommendation does not hold in the updated tool version.

original_authors: Zhang, M.; Arcuri, A.
original_title: Adaptive hypermutation for search-based system test generation: a study on REST APIs with EvoMaster
original_journal: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
description: A value of 0.5 for focusedSearchActivationTime is the optimal setting for controlling when EvoMaster transitions from broad exploratory to focused search in REST API testing
explanation: The replication found that 0.8 outperformed the original optimal value of 0.5 for focusedSearchActivationTime: 'in contrast to the conclusions of the original research (Zhang and Arcuri 2021b), a 0.5 value did not excel beyond others... 0.8 appears to be the most effective value compared to both the default and the other tested values.'

original_authors: Arcuri, A.; Galeotti, J.
original_title: Enhancing search-based testing with testability transformations for existing APIs
original_journal: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
description: A value of 0.9 for baseTaintAnalysisProbability is the most reasonable setting for dynamic taint analysis in EvoMaster REST API testing, optimizing code coverage
explanation: The replication confirmed the original finding: 'the overall results are similar to the findings of the original study as the previously suggested value (i.e., 0.9) led to higher code coverage and slightly fewer faults,' reaffirming 0.9 as the recommended setting for baseTaintAnalysisProbability.

original_authors: Gotham, K.; Risi, S.; Pickles, A.; Lord, C.
original_title: The autism diagnostic observation schedule: revised algorithms for improved diagnostic validity
original_journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
description: Revised ADOS algorithms (collapsing Social and Communication domains into Social Affect factor and adding Restricted Repetitive Behavior factor) improve diagnostic validity (sensitivity, specificity, efficiency) compared to original ADOS algorithms
explanation: The authors explicitly conclude: 'our overall finding that the diagnostic validity of the revised algorithms is better than that of the original algorithms.' The improvement was most apparent for autism cases, with less consistent improvement for non-autism ASD. The paper's title itself describes it as 'A Replication Study' of Gotham et al.'s revised algorithms.

original_authors: Gotham, K.; Risi, S.; Pickles, A.; Lord, C.
original_title: The autism diagnostic observation schedule: revised algorithms for improved diagnostic validity
original_journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
description: The revised ADOS algorithms have a two-factor structure (Social Affect and Restricted Repetitive Behavior) that fits data better than a one-factor model, with a possible three-factor solution including a Joint Attention factor
explanation: The authors confirm: 'We confirmed the factor structure proposed by [Gotham et al. 2007], and the revised algorithms were minimally influenced by age.' The two-factor model fit well (CFI 0.96-1.00, RMSEA 0.04-0.08) in cells A, B, C, with only slightly unsatisfactory fit in cell D. The three-factor model was not better than the two-factor model, supporting Gotham et al.'s decision to use the two-factor model.

original_authors: Gotham, K.; Risi, S.; Pickles, A.; Lord, C.
original_title: The autism diagnostic observation schedule: revised algorithms for improved diagnostic validity
original_journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
description: The revised ADOS algorithms reduce the influence of age and verbal/nonverbal IQ on ADOS total scores compared to the original algorithms
explanation: Age effects were confirmed as minimal and comparable to the original study. However, IQ effects were not replicated: 'we found a diminished effect of IQ (verbal and nonverbal) on revised algorithm totals in only a few cells and only with regard to the SA domain total...This is contrary to previous research [Gotham et al. 2007].' The mixed pattern (age confirmed, IQ not) makes this inconclusive overall.

original_authors: Leaf, J.; Oppenheim-Leaf, M.; Call, N.; Sheldon, J.; Sherman, J.; Taubman, M.
original_title: Comparing the teaching interaction procedure to social stories for people with autism
description: The teaching interaction procedure is more efficacious than social stories for teaching social skills to individuals with autism spectrum disorder, with mastery criterion reached on 100% of skills taught with the teaching interaction procedure but only 22% of skills taught with social stories
explanation: The authors explicitly state this study was designed to 'systematically replicate and expand upon the original [Leaf et al. 2012] study' and confirm in the Discussion that 'the results of this study were similar to the results found by [17]; participants reached mastery criterion on 100% of skills taught with the teaching interaction procedure and demonstrated little to no improvement on skills taught with social stories.' The study is classified as close extension because it preserved the core comparison methodology but expanded to a group setting and measured peer-directed rather than adult-directed performance.

original_authors: Dajani, D.; Llabre, M.; Nebel, M.; Mostofsky, S.; Uddin, L.
original_title: Heterogeneity of executive functions among comorbid neurodevelopmental disorders
description: Latent profile analysis of executive function measures in children with autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, comorbid ASD+ADHD, and typically developing children reveals three distinct EF classes ('above average', 'average', and 'impaired') that span diagnostic categories rather than mapping onto diagnostic boundaries
explanation: The authors explicitly call this a 'conceptual replication' of Dajani et al. (2016) and conclude that 'the solution observed in the present study is consistent with prior work.' They found the same three-class structure ('above average', 'average', 'impaired') with similar EF patterns across subscores, confirming the original study's main finding using only parent-report BRIEF measures in an independent ASD/TD sample.

original_authors: Lecavalier, L.; Bodfish, J.; Harrop, C.; Whitten, A.; Jones, D.; Pritchett, J.; Boyd, B.
original_title: Development of the Behavioral Inflexibility Scale for children with autism spectrum disorder and other developmental disabilities
description: The Behavioral Inflexibility Scale (BIS) is a unidimensional parent-reported measure with good to excellent levels of internal consistency, test-retest stability, and convergent validity for assessing behavioral inflexibility in autistic children
explanation: The authors explicitly conclude: 'We found that the psychometric characteristics of the BIS derived from an independent sample of autistic children replicated those reported in the [original] study.' The replication used an in-person data collection method (vs. online in the original) and included both autistic and neurotypical children, making it a close extension. Key metrics replicated closely: Cronbach's alpha = 0.98 (vs. 0.97 original), and similar convergent validity correlations with the RBS-R.

original_authors: Aston, K. I.; Krausz, C.; Laface, I.; Ruiz-Castane, E.; Carrell, D. T.
original_title: Evaluation of 172 candidate polymorphisms for association with oligozoospermia or azoospermia in a large cohort of men of European descent
description: Four SNP loci (rs5911500, rs10246939, rs2059807, rs11204546) identified in European men are associated with susceptibility to male infertility (azoospermia and oligozoospermia)
explanation: PDF Tables 2-4 and Discussion reviewed. The four European GWAS-derived SNPs (from Aston et al. 2010, per Table 2 header) showed no significant association with collective male infertility in Japanese men (Table 2: p=0.98, 0.18, 0.36, 0.18 for the four SNPs). However, subgroup analysis found rs11204546 in OR2W3 was significantly associated with oligospermia (Table 4: p=0.0037, OR=1.74). Three of four SNPs showed lower allelic risk in Japanese than European men. The Discussion frames this as partial support: OR2W3 may be 'a common risk factor in infertile men across widely different ethnicities' but the other three loci did not replicate. Classified as inconclusive because the primary analysis (collective male infertility) failed while one of four SNPs was significant only in the smaller oligospermia subgroup (n=70).

original_authors: Monaghan, S.; Blaszczynski, A.
original_title: Recall of electronic gaming machine signs: A static versus a dynamic mode of presentation
description: Dynamic (moving/scrolling) signs displayed on electronic gaming machines during play are recalled more often than static signs, with 83% vs. 15.6% free recall rates
explanation: Study 1 (lab, n=127) and Study 2 (gambling venue, n=124) both found pop-up/dynamic messages were recalled significantly more frequently and accurately than static messages. Study 1: free recall accuracy χ²(2, N=127) = 13.65, p < .001; Study 2: free recall accuracy χ²(2, N=124) = 22.72, p < .0001. Pop-up messages also had significantly greater self-reported impact on within-session thoughts and behaviors in both studies. The Discussion (p. 85) explicitly states: 'The results replicate and extend previous research findings. Similar to previous empirical laboratory studies (Cloutier et al. 2006; Floyd et al. 2006; Ladouceur and Sevigny 2003) pop-up messages appear to be superior to static signs in enhancing message recall and influencing thoughts.' The abstract also calls this a 'qualitative replication study.' This is a self-replication (same authors as [39]) that extends the original by adding message content variables (informative vs. self-appraisal vs. control) and testing in a real gambling venue (Study 2). PDF review confirmed unambiguous replication success across all measures of the dynamic vs. static comparison.

original_authors: Voight, B.; Scott, L.; Steinthorsdottir, V.
original_title: Twelve type 2 diabetes susceptibility loci identified through large-scale association analysis
description: CDKAL1 rs7754840 C allele is associated with increased risk of type 2 diabetes in European descent populations
explanation: The authors explicitly replicated the CDKAL1 rs7754840 association in Han Chinese lean subjects, finding OR = 1.54 (95% CI 1.30-1.82, P = 8.10×10⁻⁷), which remained significant after Bonferroni multiple testing correction. They state this 'matches the precise replication criteria: same marker, same allele and same phenotype definition.'

original_authors: Voight, B.; Scott, L.; Steinthorsdottir, V.
original_title: Twelve type 2 diabetes susceptibility loci identified through large-scale association analysis
description: DUSP9 rs5945326 is associated with increased risk of type 2 diabetes in European descent populations
explanation: The DUSP9 rs5945326 association showed modest significance (P = 0.02) but did not survive multiple testing correction. Moreover, the G allele appeared protective in Han Chinese (OR = 0.81) rather than being a risk factor as in Europeans (OR = 1.27), leading authors to call for further studies to 'confirm or refute' the association.

original_authors: Voight, B.; Scott, L.; Steinthorsdottir, V.
original_title: Twelve type 2 diabetes susceptibility loci identified through large-scale association analysis
description: BCL11A rs243021, CENTD2 rs1552224, and IRS1 rs7578326 are associated with type 2 diabetes risk in European descent populations
explanation: The associations of BCL11A, CENTD2, and IRS1 variants with T2D were not replicated in Han Chinese lean subjects. The authors report only CDKAL1 and DUSP9 showed any significant association, implying the remaining four SNPs (including these three) did not reach significance.

original_authors: Rosengren, A.; Jokubka, R.; Tojjar, D.
original_title: Overexpression of alpha2A-adrenergic receptors contributes to type 2 diabetes
description: ADRA2A rs553668 variant is associated with type 2 diabetes risk through overexpression of alpha2A-adrenergic receptors in European descent populations
explanation: The ADRA2A rs553668 variant was not significantly associated with T2D in Han Chinese lean subjects. Table 2 shows allele-level OR = 0.94 (95% CI 0.79-1.11), χ² = 0.54, P = 0.46, and genotype-level χ² = 0.51, P = 0.77. The paper's conclusion confirms only CDKAL1 and DUSP9 showed associations; ADRA2A clearly failed to replicate.

original_authors: Wang, L.; Zhou, F.; Li, X.; Sun, L.; Song, X.; Li, J.; Kong, J.; Qi, G.; Cui, H.; Zhang, J.; Yang, L.; et al.
original_title: Genome-wide association study of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in Chinese subjects identifies susceptibility loci at PLCE1 and C20orf54
description: PLCE1 rs2274223 variant is associated with increased risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) in Chinese populations
explanation: The replication found a significant association between PLCE1 rs2274223 GG genotype and esophageal cancer risk (adjusted OR = 1.95, 95% CI = 1.05–3.59), consistent with the original GWAS. The authors state that this finding 'is consistent with our results' from Wang et al. and Abnet et al.

original_authors: Wang, L.; Zhou, F.; Li, X.; Sun, L.; Song, X.; Li, J.; Kong, J.; Qi, G.; Cui, H.; Zhang, J.; Yang, L.; et al.
original_title: Genome-wide association study of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in Chinese subjects identifies susceptibility loci at PLCE1 and C20orf54
description: C20orf54 rs13042395 variant is associated with increased risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) in Chinese populations
explanation: No significant association was found between C20orf54 rs13042395 genotype and esophageal cancer risk (adjusted OR = 0.99, 95% CI = 0.63–1.57 for TT vs. CC). The authors state these findings 'were not consistent with one recent GWAS identified the variation of C20orf54 rs13042395 as risk factors for esophageal cancer in Chinese population [Wang et al.]'.

original_authors: Rodríguez-Rodríguez, E.; Infante, J.; Llorca, J.; Mateo, I.; Sánchez-Quintana, C.; García-Gorostiaga, I.; Sánchez-Juan, P.; Berciano, J.; Combarros, O.
original_title: Age-dependent association of KIBRA genetic variation and Alzheimer's disease risk
description: KIBRA rs17070145 polymorphism shows an age-dependent association with Alzheimer's disease risk, with the significant association found only among older seniors (>86 years) with the T-allele as a risk factor
explanation: The authors explicitly conducted 'an independent replication study' of the age-dependent KIBRA-AD association in 1,586 Han Chinese subjects, following grouping methods from Rodriguez-Rodriguez et al. and Burgess et al. They confirmed the general hypothesis that the KIBRA-AD association is age-dependent (significant only in a subgroup, not the total sample). However, the specifics diverge substantially: (1) the significant effect appeared in the YOUNG subgroup (≤74 years; p=0.045, OR=0.428) rather than the OLD subgroup as in Rodriguez-Rodriguez and Burgess; (2) the T-allele direction was protective, explicitly described as 'inconsistent with the Spanish in Rodriguez-Rodriguez et al. study.' The authors attribute these paradoxical findings to ethnic differences in T-allele frequency (75% in Asians vs. 25% in Caucasians vs. 54% in African-Americans). Reviewed PDF Tables 3 and 4: total sample showed no association (p=0.651 adjusted), old subgroup showed no association (p=0.286-0.957), only the young subgroup dominant model was significant (p=0.045).

original_authors: Aston, K.; Krausz, C.; Laface, I.; Ruiz-Castané, E.; Carrell, D.
original_title: Evaluation of 172 candidate polymorphisms for association with oligozoospermia or azoospermia in a large cohort of men of European descent
description: 172 candidate SNPs are associated with oligozoospermia or azoospermia in a Caucasian cohort of European descent
explanation: The authors tested 59 of the 172 SNPs from Aston's study in a Greek population and found that none of the original SNPs replicated — only two novel SNPs not identified in Aston's study showed statistical significance. The conclusion notes that 'neither of these two SNPs was found to be statistically significant in Aston's study dataset,' confirming a failure to replicate the original associations.

original_authors: Chen, Z.; Zhao, H.; He, L.
original_title: Genome-wide association study identifies susceptibility loci for polycystic ovary syndrome on chromosome 2p16.3, 2p21 and 9q33.3
description: Susceptibility loci on chromosomes 2p16.3 (LHCGR) and 9q33.3 (DENND1A) are associated with polycystic ovary syndrome risk in Han Chinese women
explanation: The paper tested rs2479106 and rs10818854 (DENND1A) and rs13405728 (LHCGR) from the original Han Chinese GWAS in Indian women. Only rs2479106 (DENND1A) showed a significant association with PCOS risk in NHA women (p=0.036 adjusted), but this did not survive Bonferroni correction; rs10818854 and rs13405728 showed no significant association. The authors concluded that 'some, but not all polymorphisms previously identified in Han Chinese women, could contribute to the genetic pathophysiology of PCOS in Indian women.'

original_authors: Shi, Y.; Zhao, H.; Shi, Y.
original_title: Genome-wide association study identifies eight new risk loci for polycystic ovary syndrome
description: Eight new susceptibility loci including c9orf3, RAB5B, and YAP1 are associated with polycystic ovary syndrome risk in Han Chinese women
explanation: The paper tested rs4385527 and rs3802457 (c9orf3), rs705702 (RAB5B), and rs1894116 (YAP1) from Shi et al.'s GWAS in Indian women. rs4385527 (c9orf3) and rs1894116 (YAP1) showed significant associations in NHA women that survived Bonferroni correction, while rs3802457 (c9orf3) showed no association and rs705702 (RAB5B) only trended toward significance. The mixed pattern across the four SNPs from this study leads to an inconclusive classification overall.

original_authors: Temple, J.; Choi, H.; Reuter, T.; Wolfe, D.; Taylor, C.; Madigan, S.
original_title: Childhood corporal punishment and future perpetration of physical dating violence
description: Childhood spanking/corporal punishment predicts adult dating violence perpetration, while exposure to child physical abuse does not, in a retrospective self-report study of young adults
explanation: The replication used identical measures and the same OLS regression analysis as Temple et al. (2018), but found the opposite pattern: child physical abuse significantly predicted adult dating violence (β=.276, p<.001), while spanking did not (β=.060, p=.297). The authors explicitly state: 'the reanalysis does not replicate Temple et al., 2018' and 'this study was unable to replicate previous findings by Temple and colleagues.'

original_authors: Garbarski, D.; Schaeffer, N.; Dykema, J.
original_title: The effects of response option order and question order on self-rated health
description: Response option order affects self-rated health (SRH) ratings, such that SRH is lower (worse) when response options are ordered from 'poor' to 'excellent' compared to 'excellent' to 'poor'
explanation: Study 1 (N=1,347) found a statistically significant difference in mean SRH by treatment (p<.01), with mean SRH higher (3.43) in the 'excellent' to 'poor' condition than in the 'poor' to 'excellent' condition (3.29). The authors conclude: 'The general findings are similar across the two studies, strengthening the claim that SRH is lower (worse) when the response options begin with the negative end of the scale.'

original_authors: Garbarski, D.; Schaeffer, N.; Dykema, J.
original_title: The effects of response option order and question order on self-rated health
description: Response option order affects self-rated health (SRH) ratings, such that SRH is lower (worse) when response options are ordered from 'poor' to 'excellent' compared to 'excellent' to 'poor'
explanation: Study 2 (N=499) found a statistically significant difference in mean SRH by treatment (p<.05), with mean SRH higher (3.56) in the 'excellent' to 'poor' condition than in the 'poor' to 'excellent' condition (3.35), replicating the core finding. The authors conclude: 'The general findings are similar across the two studies, strengthening the claim that SRH is lower (worse) when the response options begin with the negative end of the scale.'

original_authors: Sun, R.; Shek, D.
original_title: Life satisfaction, positive youth development, and problem behaviour among Chinese adolescents in Hong Kong
description: Positive youth development is positively related to life satisfaction and negatively related to problem behaviour among Chinese adolescents, with a bidirectional (non-recursive) relationship between life satisfaction and problem behaviour
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'the present findings are highly similar to those reported by [48], thus successfully replicating the previous findings.' The same optimal model (Model 6) was identified in both the original and replication studies, confirming the structural relationships among positive youth development, life satisfaction, and problem behaviour.

original_authors: Bonello, M.; Griffiths, M.
original_title: Analyzing consumer protection for gamblers across different online gambling operators: A descriptive study
description: Online gambling operators show inadequate responsible gambling practices and insufficient consumer protection measures when evaluated across their RG webpages, RG tool availability, and customer service interactions
explanation: The replication used identical audit methodology on 50 online gambling operators (32 overlapping with the original, 18 replaced due to closures). Table 2 provides a direct head-to-head comparison across 15 RG criteria. Improvements were found on 11 of 15 metrics (e.g., no promotional material on RG page: 12%→92%; cooling off: 72%→96%; self-exclusion: 86%→96%; CS communication re limits: 60%→86%). Four metrics were roughly unchanged. The core finding from the original — that operators have variable and often insufficient RG practices — was confirmed, with the replication additionally documenting improvements attributable to increased regulatory pressure. The authors conclude 'RG practices in the present study appear to have increased' while noting 'there are still some areas that need to be improved.' Classified as success because the replication confirms the original methodology and core descriptive finding that RG practices remain inconsistent across operators and insufficient in key areas. This is a descriptive audit study with no inferential statistics.

original_authors: Qiu, F.; Tang, R.; Zuo, X.; Shi, X.; Wei, Y.; Zheng, X.
original_title: A genome-wide association study identifies six novel risk loci for primary biliary cholangitis
description: The intergenic SNP rs10893900 at the ETS1/FLI1 locus is associated with susceptibility to primary biliary cholangitis in the Han Chinese population
explanation: The meta-analysis combining the discovery GWAS data with the independent replication cohort identified rs10893900 as a genome-wide significant locus (P = 4.55 × 10⁻⁸, OR = 1.19, 95% CI = 1.12–1.27), confirming the genetic association originally detected with suggestive evidence (P = 3.32 × 10⁻⁵) in the prior GWAS. The replication cohort alone also showed significant association (P = 3.62 × 10⁻⁴, OR = 1.16).

original_authors: Qiu, F.; Tang, R.; Zuo, X.; Shi, X.; Wei, Y.; Zheng, X.
original_title: A genome-wide association study identifies six novel risk loci for primary biliary cholangitis
description: The intronic SNP rs2246290 in FLI1 is associated with susceptibility to primary biliary cholangitis in the Han Chinese population
explanation: The replication cohort showed no significant association for rs2246290 (P = 0.42, OR = 0.95, 95% CI = 0.85–1.07), failing to confirm the suggestive signal (P = 1.50 × 10⁻⁴) observed at this variant in the original discovery GWAS.

original_authors: Shinkai, T.; Ohmori, O.; Hori, H.; Nakamura, J.
original_title: Allelic association of the neuronal nitric oxide synthase (NOS1) gene with schizophrenia
description: The rs2682826 synonymous SNP in exon 29 of the NOS1 gene is significantly associated with schizophrenia in a Japanese population
explanation: The authors explicitly conclude: 'we could not replicate the association between seven SNPs in NOS1 and schizophrenia found in several earlier studies.' Specifically regarding Shinkai et al. (2002), they state: 'although we examined more large Japanese samples than original study [15], we found no significant association with schizophrenia.'

original_authors: Fallin, M.; Lasseter, V.; Avramopoulos, D.; Nicodemus, K.; Wolyniec, P.; Mcgrath, J.
original_title: Bipolar I disorder and schizophrenia: a 440-single-nucleotide polymorphism screen of 64 candidate genes among Ashkenazi Jewish caseparent trios
description: A haplotype of four NOS1 SNPs in intron 2 (rs3782221-rs3782219-rs561712-rs3782206) is significantly associated with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder
explanation: The authors report: '[Fallin et al.] reported that significant associations of haplotypes were identified with four SNPs in intron 2 (rs3782221, rs3782219, rs561712, and rs3782206). However, no association was found in our study.' No haplotype-wise association with schizophrenia was replicated in the Japanese sample.

original_authors: Reif, A.; Strobel, S.; Ehlis, A.; Saur, A.; Jacob, D.; C
original_title: A neuronal nitric oxide synthase (NOS-I) haplotype associated with schizophrenia modifies prefrontal cortex function
description: A polymorphism (rs41279104) in the promoter region of exon 1c of NOS1 is significantly associated with schizophrenia and prefrontal brain function
explanation: Table 1 shows rs41279104 was directly tested in 542 cases vs 519 controls with no significant association (P_allele = 0.230, P_genotype = 0.436). The Discussion notes they did not test the VNTR that Reif et al. used in their haplotype, but the SNP itself (rs41279104) clearly showed no association. The overall conclusion states: 'we could not replicate the association between seven SNPs in NOS1 and schizophrenia found in several earlier studies.'

original_authors: Lambert, J.; Verbaas, I.; Harold, C.; Naj, D.; Sims, A.; Bellenguez, R.; Destafano, C.; Bis, A.
original_title: Meta-analysis of 74,046 individuals identifies 11 new susceptibility loci for Alzheimer's disease
description: The minor C allele of SORL1 rs11218343 is associated with reduced risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease in Caucasians
explanation: The authors conducted a case-control replication study in 2350 Northern Han Chinese subjects and found that the SORL1 rs11218343 C allele was protective against LOAD (recessive model: OR = 0.641, 95% CI = 0.464-0.884, P = 0.007; additive model: OR = 0.873, 95% CI = 0.765-0.996, P = 0.043). The Discussion concludes: 'our data suggest that the C allele within SORL1 rs11218343 might play a protective effect on causing LOAD in Han Chinese population.'

original_authors: Miyashita, A.; Koike, A.; Jun, G.; Wang, L.; Takahashi, S.; Matsubara, E.; Kawarabayashi, T.; Shoji, M.
original_title: SORL1 is genetically associated with late-onset Alzheimer's disease in Japanese, Koreans and Caucasians
description: The minor C allele of SORL1 rs11218343 is associated with reduced risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease in Japanese, Korean, and Caucasian populations
explanation: The authors conducted a case-control replication study in 2350 Northern Han Chinese subjects and found that the SORL1 rs11218343 C allele was protective against LOAD (recessive model: OR = 0.641, 95% CI = 0.464-0.884, P = 0.007), extending the finding to the Chinese population. The conclusion states: 'the C allele in SORL1 rs11218343 may be a protective factor for LOAD in both Caucasian and Han Chinese.'

original_authors: Chang, Y.; Liu, P.; Lee, W.; Chang, T.; Jiang, Y.; Li, H.
original_title: Common variation in the fat mass and obesity-associated (FTO) gene confers risk of obesity and modulates BMI in the Chinese population
description: The A allele of the FTO rs9939609 SNP is significantly associated with increased risk of obesity (BMI ≥ 30) in a Taiwanese population
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'Our study is the first, to date, to have successfully replicated the association of the FTO rs9939609 SNP with the risk of obesity among Taiwanese individuals.' The replication found a significant genotypic association (P=0.021), with adjusted OR=9.86 (95% CI: 1.31-74.09, P=0.026) for the AA vs AT+TT genotype comparison.

original_authors: Song, H.; Ramus, S.; Tyrer, J.
original_title: A genome-wide association study identifies a new ovarian cancer susceptibility locus on 9p22.2
description: The SNP rs3814113 on 9p22.2 is associated with susceptibility to epithelial ovarian cancer across all histological subtypes
explanation: The authors found significant p_trend values for rs3814113 (9p22) with all EOT subtypes (p=0.010) and specifically for serous histological subtypes (p=0.006), and a significant association with serous ovarian carcinoma in the dominant model (OR=0.532, 95% CI=0.342-0.827, p=0.005, p_corr=0.035), consistent with the original GWAS finding.

original_authors: Goode, E.; Chenevix-Trench, G.; Song, H.
original_title: A genome-wide association study identifies susceptibility loci for ovarian cancer at 2q31 and 8q24
description: SNPs rs10088218 and rs10098821 on 8q24, rs2665390 on 3q25 (TIPARP), rs2072590 on 2q31 (HOXD-AS1), and rs9303542 on 17q21 (SKAP1) are associated with susceptibility to epithelial ovarian cancer
explanation: Of the 5 SNPs from this GWAS (rs2072590, rs2665390, rs10088218, rs10098821, rs9303542), 4 showed no significant association at all (p_trend values of 0.652, 0.715, 0.120, and 0.162 respectively). Only rs10098821 reached nominal significance (p_trend=0.014 for all EOTs; dominant model OR=0.576, p=0.008) but did not survive Bonferroni correction (threshold p=0.007). The authors acknowledged the small sample size may have caused missed associations. Overall the GWAS findings from Goode et al. were not confirmed in this population.

original_authors: Couch, F.; Gaudet, M.; Antoniou, A.
original_title: Common variants at 19p13 are associated with susceptibility to ovarian cancer
description: SNPs rs8170 and rs2363956 on 19p13 (ANKLE1) are associated with susceptibility to serous ovarian cancer
explanation: The rs2363956 (ANKLE1) SNP on 19p13 showed no significant association in any analysis. Table 2 confirms: All EOTs p_trend=0.399, serous p_trend=0.139, with no significant p-values across any histological subtype, inheritance model, clinical stage, or histological grade. The original GWAS specifically found significance for serous ovarian cancer (Bolton et al. 2010), but even the serous subtype showed no signal here (dominant OR=1.531, p=0.137; allelic p=0.169).

original_authors: Köteles, F.; Szemerszky, R.; Gubányi, M.; Körmendi, J.; Szekrényesi, C.; Lloyd, R.
original_title: Idiopathic environmental intolerance attributed to electromagnetic fields (IEI-EMF) and electrosensibility (ES)—are they connected?
original_journal: International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health
description: Individuals with IEI-EMF (idiopathic environmental intolerance attributed to electromagnetic fields) show a better-than-random detection performance (higher d' index) for a 50-Hz 0.5-mT magnetic field compared to controls who do not differ from random guessing
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'The most surprising finding of our earlier research, namely the better than random detection performance of the IEI-EMF group, was replicated in the current study, even the magnitude of the d′ indices was quite similar (M=0.296 vs 0.280).' The IEI-EMF group showed a significant d' > 0 (t(48)=2.131, p=0.038) while the control group did not.

original_authors: Köteles, F.; Szemerszky, R.; Gubányi, M.; Körmendi, J.; Szekrényesi, C.; Lloyd, R.
original_title: Idiopathic environmental intolerance attributed to electromagnetic fields (IEI-EMF) and electrosensibility (ES)—are they connected?
original_journal: International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health
description: Individuals with IEI-EMF show a significantly higher response bias (lower β index) toward assuming the presence of the magnetic field compared to controls
explanation: The authors state in the Discussion: 'Participants in the IEI-EMF group of our previous experiment showed a significantly higher bias toward the presence of the MF than the controls. In the current study, however, no such difference between the two groups was found.' The β comparison yielded t(104)=-0.380, p=0.705.

original_authors: Witkiewitz, K.; Bowen, S.; Douglas, H.; Hsu, S.
original_title: Mindfulness-based relapse prevention for substance craving
description: Self-reported mindfulness (a latent factor comprising Acting with Awareness and Nonjudgment FFMQ subscales and a modified Acceptance and Action Questionnaire) significantly mediates the effect of mindfulness-based relapse prevention (MBRP) on reductions in substance use craving following treatment
explanation: The authors explicitly report: 'Results from the secondary analyses indicated the test of mindfulness as a mechanism of behavior change in the association between MBRP and craving failed to replicate in Study 2.' The a-path (MBRP → mindfulness latent factor) was not significant in Study 2 (β = -0.12, p = .053) and the indirect effect was also non-significant (p = .073), confirming a failed replication.

original_authors: Ballantyne, C.; Hunter, P.; Potter, G.; Myge, I.
original_title: Mindfulness and perceptions of physical health: The mediating role of perceived stress
original_journal: Canadian Journal of Behavioural Science / Revue Canadienne Des Sciences Du Comportement
description: Four facets of trait mindfulness (describing, non-judging, non-reactivity, acting with awareness) are negatively associated with physical symptoms of stress, with this relationship partially mediated by lower perceived stress, and non-judging showing the strongest effect
explanation: The Discussion explicitly states: 'we replicated the results of [Ballantyne et al.] and [Roberts & Danoff-Burg] by showing significant mediation effects for four out of five facets of mindfulness (describing, non-judging, non-reactivity, and acting with awareness). Non-judging showed the strongest effect, as predicted.' The current study extends the original by using SEM to test all facets simultaneously while controlling for covariates.

original_authors: Roberts, K.; Danoff-Burg, S.
original_title: Mindfulness and health behaviors: Is paying attention good for you
description: Higher trait mindfulness is associated with better perceived physical functioning in college students, with perceived stress partially mediating this relationship
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'we replicated the results of [Roberts & Danoff-Burg] and [Ballantyne et al.]' and confirm the stress-buffering effect of trait mindfulness. The current study uses a different analytic approach (SEM with five separate mindfulness facets and covariates) compared to the original's simpler mediation analysis, making this a conceptual replication.

original_authors: Ko, A.; Tu, H.; Liu, T.; Chang, J.; Yuo, C.; Chiang, S.
original_title: ALPK1 genetic regulation and risk in relation to gout
description: Three SNPs in the ALPK1 gene (rs11726117, rs231247, rs231253) are associated with gout susceptibility in Taiwanese Han and Taiwan aboriginal populations
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'the present study detected no significant association between ALPK1 and gout,' testing the same SNP (rs11726117) in a Japanese population (903 cases, 1,302 controls) and finding p = 0.44 for the allele frequency association, compared to the original significant association reported in Taiwanese populations.

original_authors: Himmelstein, D.
original_title: The history of publishing delays
original_journal: Satoshi Village: the blog of Daniel Himmelstein
description: Mean time from manuscript submission to acceptance across 3,475 biomedical journals in PubMed was approximately 100 days, with an additional ~25-day lag between acceptance and PubMed publication
explanation: The authors explicitly replicated Himmelstein's bibliometric methodology but applied it to health professions education (HPE) journals. They found mean publication time of 263.55 days and acceptance time of 180.93 days — more than twice the ~100-day benchmark from the original study. The Discussion states results are 'over twice as long as the 100-day benchmark published by Himmelstein,' indicating the original finding does not hold in the HPE context.

original_authors: Wald, H.; Borkan, J.; Taylor, J.
original_title: Fostering and evaluating reflective capacity in medical education: developing the REFLECT rubric for assessing reflective writing
description: The REFLECT rubric for assessing reflective writing produces good inter-rater reliability characteristics (ICC single measures = 0.632, with a range of 0.376–0.748 across developmental iterations)
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'We did not replicate the reliability characteristics presented in the original REFLECT article.' Their replication, conducted at a different institution with a different participant mix, yielded poor ICC values (overall ICC = 0.448) compared to the original's best ICC of 0.748.

original_authors: Brown, J.; Petronis, K.; Bate, A.; Zhang, F.; Dashevsky, I.; Kulldorff, M.
original_title: Drug adverse event detection in health plan data using the gamma poisson shrinker and comparison to the tree-based scan statistic
description: The tree-based scan statistic (TBSS) applied to HMO Research Network data detects signals of disproportionate recording (SDRs) for adverse events among users of terbinafine and itraconazole
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as a 'conceptual replication' with different methods and data. They found that only the digestive system SDR for terbinafine replicated (4 of 11 HMO SDRs, or 36.4%, were also identified in Optum data), stating 'other SDRs from the previous publications were not replicated' and noting 'broad consistency, but far from perfect concordance.'

original_authors: Kulldorff, M.; Dashevsky, I.; Avery, T.; Chan, A.; Davis, R.; Graham, D.
original_title: Drug safety data mining with a tree-based scan statistic
description: The tree-based scan statistic (TBSS) applied to HMO Research Network data identifies signals of disproportionate recording (SDRs) for adverse events among terbinafine and itraconazole users
explanation: The authors explicitly call this a 'conceptual replication' of both Kulldorff et al. and Brown et al. using different data and methods. Results showed partial overlap: the digestive system SDR for terbinafine replicated, but most other SDRs from the original HMO Research Network analysis did not, with authors noting 'the amount of discordance between our results and those from Kulldorff et al. seems notable.'

original_authors: Ara, R.; Blake, L.; Gray, L.; Hernandez, M.; Crowther, M.; Dunkley, A.
original_title: What is the clinical effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of using drugs in treating obese patients in primary care? A systematic review
description: Health economic Markov model (13 health states) comparing orlistat, rimonabant, and sibutramine versus placebo for obese adults in a UK primary care setting, reporting cost-utility outcomes (costs and QALYs) over a lifetime horizon
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'case study 1 needs to be rated as a failure in reproducing results' due to strong variation in incremental QALYs and failure to present acceptable ICER results. The non-successful reproduction was attributed in part to the model's lack of reported clinical event results.

original_authors: Au, N.; Marsden, G.; Mortimer, D.; Lorgelly, P.
original_title: The cost-effectiveness of shopping to a predetermined grocery list to reduce overweight and obesity
description: Health economic Markov model (9 health states) evaluating the cost-effectiveness of shopping to a predetermined grocery list (standard behavioral therapy with meal plans and shopping lists versus standard behavioral therapy alone or no intervention) for reducing overweight and obesity in a UK adult population
explanation: The authors report that 'the proposed combination of success criteria were all clearly fulfilled for case studies 2, 3, and 4,' and case study 2 achieved a successful reproduction. The CE coordinate plane could be reproduced and variation in costs was < 5%.

original_authors: Caro, J.; Stillman, O.; Danel, A.; Getsios, D.; Mcewan, P.
original_title: Cost effectiveness of rimonabant use in patients at increased cardiometabolic risk: estimates from a Markov model
description: Health economic Markov model (5 health states) evaluating the cost-effectiveness of rimonabant versus diet and exercise for obese patients at increased cardiometabolic risk in a UK adult population over a lifetime horizon
explanation: The authors explicitly state that 'the proposed combination of success criteria were all clearly fulfilled for case studies 2, 3, and 4.' Case study 3 showed the best fit of reproduction results, with ICER point estimates in the CE coordinate plane almost overlapping with the original.

original_authors: Meads, D.; Hulme, C.; Hall, P.; Hill, A.
original_title: The cost-effectiveness of primary care referral to a UK commercial weight loss programme
description: Health economic Markov model (9 health states) evaluating the cost-effectiveness of referral to a UK commercial weight loss programme (Slimming World) versus best supportive care for obese adults in UK primary care over a lifetime horizon
explanation: The authors explicitly state that 'the proposed combination of success criteria were all clearly fulfilled for case studies 2, 3, and 4.' Case study 4 showed among the best reproduction fits, with ICER point estimates almost overlapping in the CE coordinate plane.

original_authors: Roth, S.; Zmuda, J.; Cauley, J.
original_title: Vitamin D receptor genotype is associated with fat-free mass and sarcopenia in elderly men
description: VDR FokI F/F genotype is associated with a twofold higher risk for sarcopenia and lower fat-free mass in elderly men
explanation: The replication found no significant sarcopenia association in men (contradicting the original twofold risk finding), but did find a significant 1.3-fold increased odds of sarcopenia in women (Fok1 FF vs f-allele carriers, 95% CI 1.2-1.4), a group not tested in the original study. The authors conclude 'the data indicate a generally modest contribution of this gene with sarcopenia risk,' reflecting partial and mixed support for the original findings.

original_authors: Byrne, B.; Rehfeldt, R.; Aguirre, A.
original_title: Evaluating the effectiveness of the stimulus pairing observation procedure and multiple exemplar instruction on tact and listener responses in children with autism
description: The stimulus-pairing observation procedure (SPOP) and multiple exemplar instruction (MEI) are effective in establishing emergent tact and listener responses in children with autism spectrum disorder
explanation: The authors explicitly describe their study as 'a systematic replication of Byrne, Rehfeldt, and Aguirre (2014)' with modifications including additional SPOP sessions if needed and selecting participants with better prerequisite skills. All three participants met mastery criterion for tact and listener relations following SPOP instruction, demonstrating SPOP effectiveness — though the current study showed faster acquisition (one session only) compared to the original, which needed MEI for most participants.

original_authors: Charlop-Christy, M.; Daneshvar, S.
original_title: Using video modeling to teach perspective taking to children with autism
description: Video modeling can teach children with autism spectrum disorder to pass false-belief tasks (hide-and-seek and Sally-Anne tasks), with generalization to untrained stimulus variations
explanation: The authors explicitly state this is 'a systematic replication' extending Charlop-Christy & Daneshvar (2003) and LeBlanc et al. (2003), replacing video modeling with live people and a natural environment setting. All three participants successfully learned the targeted false-belief tasks and generalized to the untrained Sally-Anne task, with the authors concluding 'these results extend previous research by demonstrating that training these tasks using straightforward behavioral intervention strategies in the natural environment was effective.'

original_authors: Leblanc, L.; Coates, A.; Daneshvar, S.; Charlop-Christy, M.; Morris, C.; Lancaster, B.
original_title: Using video modeling and reinforcement to teach perspective-taking skills to children with autism
description: Video modeling combined with reinforcement can teach children with autism to pass false-belief tasks (hide-and-seek and M&Ms tasks), with generalization to stimulus variations and the untrained Sally-Anne task
explanation: The paper explicitly describes itself as 'a systematic replication' extending LeBlanc et al. (2003), using the same tasks (hide-and-seek and M&Ms) but with live people in a natural environment instead of video modeling. All three participants mastered the targeted tasks and generalized to the Sally-Anne posttest, consistent with the original study's findings.

original_authors: Kodak, T.; Halbur, M.; Bergmann, S.; Costello, D.; Benitez, B.; Olsen, M.; Gorgan, E.; Cliett, T.
original_title: A comparison of stimulus set size on tact training for children with autism spectrum disorder
description: Larger stimulus set sizes (6 and 12 stimuli) produce faster tact acquisition than smaller set sizes (3 and 4 stimuli) in discrete trial instruction for children with ASD
explanation: The replication found the opposite pattern from Kodak et al.: set-size-3 was consistently most efficient for acquisition for all three participants. The authors explicitly state: 'our results contrasted with Kodak et al.'s findings that the larger set-size-twelve was more efficient than the small set-size-three in skill acquisition.' The reversal is attributed to methodological differences in acquisition criteria.

original_authors: Vladescu, J.; Gureghian, D.; Goodwyn, L.; Campanaro, A.
original_title: Comparing skill acquisition under different stimulus set sizes with adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: A replication
description: Smaller stimulus set sizes (3 and 6 stimuli) are more efficient than larger set sizes (12 stimuli) for tact acquisition in adolescents with ASD when controlling the number of independent correct responses required to meet criterion across conditions
