description: Metabolomic abnormalities (including cerebral folate deficiency and tetrahydrobiopterin deficiency) are significantly more prevalent in patients with treatment refractory depression than in healthy controls, and are identifiable via CSF and peripheral metabolic testing
explanation: The authors explicitly framed this study as a replication of their 2016 case-control study [26], stating 'We hypothesized that we would replicate our earlier findings.' The Conclusions confirm success: 'Our initial case control study [26] and this replication CNS-specific metabolomic survey are the first to systematically evaluate abnormalities...'; 48% of treatment refractory depression patients (67/141) showed metabolomic abnormalities compared to 0% of healthy controls, consistent with the original finding of abnormalities in 21/33 patients and none in controls.

original_authors: He, A.; Kon, M.; Arunachalam, S.
original_title: Linguistic context in verb learning: Less is sometimes more
description: Children learning English show better novel verb acquisition when sentences have unmodified subjects (e.g., 'the man is pilking') compared to modified subjects (e.g., 'the tall man is pilking'), because the processing load of modified noun phrases reduces resources available for verb learning
explanation: The authors explicitly label this a 'conceptual replication' and their results confirm the key finding: Korean-learning preschoolers, like English-learning toddlers, demonstrated above-chance verb learning only in the unmodified-subject condition (p = .02), with all three modified-subject conditions yielding chance-level performance. The Discussion states: 'This replication of the finding in [He et al., 2020] for younger English learners establishes the appropriateness of the paradigm for Korean-acquiring preschoolers.'

original_authors: Narayan, A.; Ghosh Ippen, C.; Harris, W.; Lieberman, A.
original_title: Assessing angels in the nursery: A pilot study of childhood memories of benevolent caregiving as protective influences
description: More positive and elaborated angel memories (childhood memories of feeling loved by caregivers) buffer the association between mothers' childhood maltreatment and their adult PTSD symptoms
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'This study replicates and extends published pilot findings showing the protective role of benevolent childhood memories with caregivers...The present study replicated these findings.' The moderation interaction was significant (b = −.15, p = .05), consistent with the original study's finding.

original_authors: Asendorpf, J.; Motti-Stefanidi, F.
original_title: Mediated disposition-environment transactions: the DAE model
description: Personality traits (dispositions) causally dominate conduct and self-esteem with peers (adaptations), which in turn mediate the association between personality traits and peer acceptance/rejection (environment) in adolescents, as specified by the DAE model
explanation: The authors explicitly state this is a 'conceptual replication of the DAE-model' using different variables (neuroticism, disagreeableness, unconscientiousness; social problems; parent-child relationship quality) and report that 'results partially support the DAE hypotheses' — some hypothesized associations were found (D→E and A→E) but key DAE predictions (co-influence of D and E on A, causal dominance of D over A, and mediation effects) were not supported.

original_authors: Glick, Ira; Davis, John; Zamora, Daisy
original_title: Should antipsychotic medications for schizophrenia be given for a lifetime? A naturalistic, long-term follow-up study
description: Better medication adherence to antipsychotics is a statistically significant predictor of better long-term global outcome and life satisfaction in patients with chronic schizophrenia
explanation: The replication found mixed results: medication adherence was significantly associated with blind clinician's ratings of global outcome (P=0.03) and GAFS (P=0.05), but not with non-blind clinician global outcome (P=0.26) or patient life satisfaction (P=0.54). The authors note 'the effect of medication adherence was weaker than observed in our study from an academic sample' and characterize the study as 'not inconsistent with' the original recommendation while urging caution.

original_authors: Havnen, A.; Hansen, B.; Öst, L.; Kvale, G.
original_title: Concentrated ERP delivered in a group setting: an effectiveness study
original_journal: Journal of Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders
description: Concentrated Exposure and Response Prevention (cET) delivered in a group format over four consecutive days produces significant reductions in OCD symptom severity (Y-BOCS scores) with high recovery rates in an outpatient clinical sample
explanation: The authors explicitly conclude: 'This study shows that cET was successfully replicated in a new patient sample treated by different therapists than the original study.' No significant differences were found between the two studies on any primary or secondary outcome measures (Y-BOCS scores, recovery rates, or occupational impairment).

original_authors: Sullivan, K.; Woods, S.; Bucks, R.; Loft, S.; Weinborn, M.
original_title: Intraindividual variability in neurocognitive performance is associated with time-based prospective memory in older adults
original_journal: Journal of Clinical and Experimental Neuropsychology
description: Higher intraindividual variability in neurocognitive performance (IIV-dispersion across the RBANS battery) is negatively associated with time-based prospective memory performance in healthy older adults, with a small but independent effect
explanation: The authors explicitly designed the study as a 'conceptual replication' of Sullivan et al. (2018), testing the same hypothesis with different cognitive batteries and PM measures in HIV populations. The Discussion states: 'The magnitude, direction, and independence of the association between IIV-dispersion and time-based PM in the laboratory parallels prior findings using the RBANS and the MIsT in older healthy Australians [49],' and the authors conclude that 'these findings suggest that variability in performance across a cognitive battery contributes to laboratory-based PM accuracy.'

original_authors: Evans, C.; Baumberger-Henry, M.; Schwartz, R.
original_title: Nursing students' transfer of learning during a disaster tabletop exercise
description: Senior student nurses can transfer their learning to novel disaster-scenario decisions (patient disposition recommendations) during a tabletop exercise, demonstrating basic disaster and medical-surgical knowledge
explanation: The paper is explicitly titled 'A Replication Study' and uses the same instruments (DKT, MATRIX, TAQ) and disaster-scenario tabletop exercise paradigm from the original study (ref 6). The replication was extended to 2 Mid-Atlantic universities (N=129). The conclusion states students 'could safely transfer their learning to most decisions during a novel circumstance with a high degree of risk,' consistent with the original findings. The pattern of results matches: positive attitudes (TAQ means 2.7-4.4), strong TOL for most DKT topics and MATRIX physical/functional assessments, with specific gaps in PPE knowledge and complex patient dispositions (pain DI=.28, hyponatremia DI=.30). The study uses descriptive/DI-based statistics rather than hypothesis testing, so no direct statistical comparison to the original is possible, but the overall findings clearly support the same conclusions.

original_authors: Matsumoto, H.; Takei, N.; Saito, F.; Kachi, K.; Mori, N.
original_title: Childhood-onset schizophrenia and obstetric complications: a case-control study
description: Exposure to obstetric complications (OCs) is associated with an increased risk of developing childhood-onset schizophrenia (COS), with an odds ratio of approximately 3.5
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion that 'the OR (odds ratio) for the development of the disorder was 3.2, which was almost identical to that demonstrated in our previous study (OR = 3.5),' and conclude that 'the data from these two independent studies strongly support an association between OCs and COS.' The replication used the same OC scale, same case-control design, and same hospital catchment area, but tested a different age group (14-15 years vs. <14 years) to ensure sample independence.

original_authors: Perez, F.; Rivera, V.; Meyer, J.; Gay, J.; Taylor, R.; Mathew, N.
original_title: Analysis of intellectual and cognitive performance in patients with multi-infarct dementia, vertebrobasilar insufficiency with dementia and Alzheimer's disease
original_journal: Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery and Psychiatry
description: Patients with Alzheimer's disease and multi-infarct dementia show significant differences in cognitive and intellectual performance on the WAIS, with a discriminant function analysis classifying 74% of patients correctly based on individual WAIS scores
explanation: The paper is explicitly titled 'A Replication Study' and the abstract states 'Successful replication was obtained.' The Discussion confirms: 'The findings of the first sample are consistent with previous results reported by this laboratory (Perez et al., 1975a)' and the discriminant function hit rates (81% and 100%) exceeded those of the original study (74%).

original_authors: Storozheva, Z.; Kirenskaya, A.; Lazarev, I.; Novototskii-Vlasov, V.; Samylkin, D.; Fastovtsov, G.
original_title: Prepulse modification of the acoustic startle reaction in healthy subjects and patients with schizophrenia
description: Schizophrenia patients show deficient prepulse inhibition (PPI) of the acoustic startle response at lead intervals of 60 ms and 120 ms compared to healthy controls in a Russian population
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'In agreement with our previous results [45] this replication study revealed deficit of PPI in SCH group at LI 60 and 120 ms,' directly confirming the replication succeeded. The current study used the same ASR/PPI protocol with a larger sample (28 patients + 25 controls vs. 16 + 16 in the original).

original_authors: Baughman, H.; Schwartz, S.; Schermer, J.; Veselka, L.; Petrides, K.; Vernon, P.
original_title: A behaviouralgenetic study of alexithymia and its relationships with trait emotional intelligence
description: Individual differences in alexithymia are attributable to additive genetic and non-shared environmental factors only (no shared environmental contribution)
explanation: The replication found an additional shared environmental factor that was not present in the original study. The authors state: 'These findings are in contrast to those of [5], where only significant genetic and non-shared environmental factors were noted.' The original used small samples; the larger replication revealed a shared environmental component.

original_authors: Baughman, H.; Schwartz, S.; Schermer, J.; Veselka, L.; Petrides, K.; Vernon, P.
original_title: A behaviouralgenetic study of alexithymia and its relationships with trait emotional intelligence
description: Phenotypic correlations between alexithymia and trait emotional intelligence are entirely attributable to correlated genetic and correlated non-shared environmental factors
explanation: The bivariate behavioral genetic results were successfully replicated. The authors state: 'Our bivariate BG analyses revealed that the phenotypic correlations between trait EI and alexithymia are entirely attributable to genetic and non-shared environmental factors. These results provide a valuable replication of [5] small-sample pilot study, in which similar results were reported.'

original_authors: Trivedi, D.
original_title: Discovery of volatile biomarkers of Parkinson's disease from sebum
description: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) measured from sebum using TD-GC-MS show a differential profile between Parkinson's disease patients and controls, with a correct classification rate of ~86% using PLS-DA
explanation: The paper explicitly calls itself a 'replication study' in the abstract and conclusion: 'Our results validate previous findings that VOCs measured from skin have a differential profile in Parkinson's disease.' The replication achieved an 84.4% correct classification rate, comparable to the original study's 86%, using a different instrument and independent patient samples.

original_authors: Qiu, Y.; Cai, G.; Su, M.; Chen, T.; Zheng, X.; Xu, Y.; Ni, Y.; Zhao, A.; Xu L.; Cai, S.; Jia, W.
original_title: Serum metabolite profiling of human colorectal cancer using GC-TOFMS and UPLC-QTOFMS
description: Serum metabolite profiling using GC-TOFMS and UPLC-QTOFMS can identify a distinct metabolic signature that distinguishes colorectal cancer patients from healthy controls
explanation: The authors explicitly designed this as a 'follow-up replication study' of their previous CRC metabonomics work, using the same analytical platforms (GC-TOFMS and UPLC-QTOFMS) on a new patient cohort. Their conclusion states: 'We confirmed that serum based metabonomics is able to discriminate CRC patients from healthy controls, reassuring us about the feasibility of developing a new diagnostic tool for CRC with a serum metabolite signature.' While not all individual markers replicated (70.1% of previously identified markers were also significant in the new cohort), the core finding was confirmed.

original_authors: Drake, R.; Becker, D.; Anthony, W.
original_title: A research induction group for clients entering a mental health research project
description: A research induction group (four sessions of education and discussion about study procedures) for mental health clients improves informed consent, increases participation rates, and reduces attrition in a supported employment research study
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'This study replicated the success of the research induction group procedure in our earlier New Hampshire study.' The replication used the same core procedure in a new inner-city setting with predominantly African-American clients (vs. rural, culturally homogeneous), testing generalizability across populations and contexts.

original_authors: Barker, S.; Barron, N.; McFarland, B.; Bigelow, D.; Carnahan, T.
original_title: A community ability scale for chronically mentally ill consumers: Part II. Applications
description: Lower scores on the Multnomah Community Ability Scale (MCAS) predict subsequent involuntary psychiatric hospitalization among clients with severe mental illness in an urban community mental health setting
explanation: The statewide replication found a highly significant trend (χ² = 42.46, p < .0001) in the same direction as the original, and the regression coefficients were not significantly different between the two samples (heterogeneity χ² = 0.59, NS). The authors conclude: 'This study replicated the predictive validation of a level of functioning measure' and 'the results of both validation studies were quite similar.'

original_authors: Kozel, F.A.; Revell, L.J.; Lorberbaum, J.P.; Shastri, A.; Elhai, J.D.; Horner, M.D.
original_title: A pilot study of functional MRI brain correlates of deception in healthy young men
original_journal: Journal of Neuropsychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences
description: Deception (lying vs. truth-telling) activates specific brain regions (right orbitofrontal, inferior frontal, middle frontal cortex, cingulate gyrus, and left middle frontal) as measured by fMRI BOLD signal
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'This study replicates the group analysis findings from a previous study using fMRI to detect deception.' The group analysis revealed significant activation in 5 regions consistent with the prior study (right anterior cingulate, right inferior frontal, right orbitofrontal, right middle frontal, and left middle temporal), with a more conservative statistical threshold.

original_authors: Volling, B.; Blandon, A.; Gorvine, B.
original_title: Maternal and paternal gentle guidance and young children's compliance from a within-family perspective
description: Parental gentle guidance (mothers' and fathers'), coparenting interactions, and differential parental treatment predict young children's committed compliance, situational compliance, and passive noncompliance during a family clean-up task from a within-family perspective
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'Several of the results were replicated with our older sample' but key findings differed: the maternal gatekeeping interaction (low maternal guidance → positive father-child association for younger siblings' committed compliance) was not replicated, and the coparenting interaction predicting older siblings' committed compliance also did not replicate. The abstract and Discussion both acknowledge this mixed pattern of replication.

original_authors: Schwabe, L.; Wolf, O.
original_title: Socially evaluated cold pressor stress after instrumental learning favors habits over goal-directed action
description: Stressed participants continue to perform instrumental responses for a liquid outcome even after it has been devalued through a selective satiation procedure, indicating that stress causes a shift from goal-directed to habitual behavioral control
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'the current study did not replicate the original findings. Instead, it showed a devaluation effect in both the control and the stress condition.' The key Condition × Value interaction was non-significant (F(1.89, 124.33) = 1.10, p = .333, η²p = .016), providing no support for habitual processing under stress with taste aversion as the devaluation method.

original_authors: Raby, K.; Cicchetti, D.; Carlson, E.; Egeland, B.
original_title: Genetic contributions to continuity and change in attachment security: A prospective, longitudinal investigation from infancy to young adulthood
original_journal: Journal of Child Psychiatry and Psychology
description: OXTR rs53576 genotype moderates the stability of attachment security from infancy to adulthood, such that individuals homozygous for the G allele (G/G genotype) show greater continuity between infant attachment security and adult attachment representations (as measured by the Adult Attachment Interview) compared to A allele carriers
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'the current study failed to replicate the evidence that individuals homozygous for the rs53576 G allele exhibit more stability in attachment security from early childhood to young adulthood compared to A allele carriers.' All two-way interactions between early childhood attachment security and OXTR variants were non-significant across all adult attachment outcomes examined.

original_authors: Van Aken, M.; Asendorpf, J.
original_title: Support by parents, classmates, friends and siblings in preadolescence: Covariation and compensation across relationships
original_journal: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships
description: Friend support from the most supportive classmate moderates the association between maternal social support and adolescent self-esteem, such that high classmate support buffers against the negative effects of low maternal support on self-esteem (conjunction effect)
explanation: The replication explicitly failed to find the hypothesized moderation: 'Data from multiple studies, analyzed collectively and separately, were unable to replicate previous findings suggesting that friend social support moderates associations between mother-child relationship quality and concurrent adolescent self-esteem.' The interaction between mother support and friend support was non-significant (F_mean(1,1466)=0.49, p=0.83) in the replication, contrasting with the original conjunction effect, and the effect sizes for the interaction were near zero.

original_authors: Gauze, C.; Bukowski, W.; Aquan-Assee, J.; Sippola, L.
original_title: Interactions between family environment and friendship and associations with self-perceived well-being during adolescence
description: Friendship quality moderates associations between family environment (adaptability and cohesion) and adolescent self-esteem, such that high friendship quality buffers against the negative effects of poor family relationships on self-esteem (threshold effect)
explanation: The replication failed to find the hypothesized moderation: 'There were no statistically significant two- or three-way interactions' and 'in neither case was there any suggestion of the threshold effect reported in the original study.' For the key interaction terms, the replication effect sizes were drastically smaller than the originals (family adaptability × friend support: replication f²<0.0002 vs. original f²=0.06; family cohesion × friend support: replication f²<0.00003 vs. original f²=0.07).

original_authors: Moffitt, T.; Arseneault, L.; Belsky, D.; Dickson, N.; Hancox, R.; Harrington, H.; Houts, R.; Poulton, R.; Roberts, B.; Ross, S.; Sears, M.; Thomson, W.; Caspi, A.
original_title: A gradient of childhood self-control predicts health, wealth, and public safety
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
description: Childhood self-control problems (impulsive, hyperactive, inattentive, and impulsive-aggressive behaviors) predict poorer adult financial status, worse health, and greater criminal activity decades later
explanation: The authors explicitly conducted 'two conceptual replications' of Moffitt et al. (2011) using U.S. (n=1,168) and U.K. (n=16,506) longitudinal cohort studies. Their Discussion concludes: 'Our analyses produced remarkably similar results; in some cases, coefficients were nearly identical to those reported by Moffitt and colleagues (2011),' with findings on educational attainment, criminal activity, health, and financial outcomes consistently replicated across both new cohorts.

original_authors: Bowers, E.; Li, Y.; Kiely, M.; Brittian, A.; Lerner, J.; Lerner, R.
original_title: The five Cs model of positive youth development: A longitudinal analysis of confirmatory factor structure and measurement invariance
description: The Five Cs model of Positive Youth Development (Caring, Character, Competence, Confidence, Connection) can be measured as a valid bifactor structure with longitudinal measurement invariance across middle adolescence
explanation: The authors explicitly frame their study as a 'conceptual replication' of the Five Cs bifactor model in a Mexican-origin sample using novel measures, and report that all hypotheses were supported: the bifactor structure fit well, scalar invariance was established, and cultural orientation predicted PYD — concluding 'evidence validating the Five Cs model of PYD' and that 'these findings uphold the robust nature of the Five Cs theoretical constructs by evincing that they are not inherently dependent on original measurement procedures.'

original_authors: Cohen, G.; Garcia, J.; Apfel, N.; Master, A.
original_title: Reducing the racial achievement gap: A social-psychological intervention
description: Brief self-affirmation writing exercises (reflecting on personally important values) conducted several times during 7th grade reduce the racial achievement gap in GPA for African American and Hispanic students
explanation: The authors state: 'Concerning our first research question, therefore, we found no evidence of treatment benefits for the targeted population in the new study.' Effect estimates for 7th grade GPA (d=-0.002) and 8th grade GPA (d=-0.072) were not statistically different from zero, and the Discussion confirms: 'we found no effects of the intervention for cohort 2.'

original_authors: Borman, G.; Grigg, J.; Hanselman, P.
original_title: An effort to close achievement gaps at scale through self-affirmation
description: A large-scale district-wide implementation of self-affirmation writing exercises in 7th grade produces significant positive impacts on GPA for potentially threatened (Black and Hispanic) students across 11 middle schools
explanation: The current study (cohort 2) was conducted in the same district and schools as Borman et al. (cohort 1), by the same research team with the same protocols. Cohort 1 showed d=0.152 for 8th grade GPA, while cohort 2 showed d=-0.072; the authors report 'we rejected the null hypothesis that impacts were equal in both studies' (p=0.013), establishing a clear failure to replicate.

original_authors: Maccann, C.; Joseph, D.; Newman, D.; Roberts, R.
original_title: Emotional intelligence is a second-stratum factor of intelligence: evidence from hierarchical and bifactor models
description: Ability emotional intelligence, measured by the MSCEIT, can be represented as a hierarchical second-stratum factor within the Cattell-Horn-Carroll (CHC) model of intelligence, alongside fluid intelligence, crystallised intelligence, and other broad cognitive abilities
explanation: The authors explicitly frame the study as 'a conceptual replication of the MacCann et al. (2014) analyses' using alternative non-proprietary measures instead of the MSCEIT, and conclude: 'the results of the current study are consistent with [the original] in suggesting that ability EI is best considered as a hierarchically structured (loaded emotion perception, understanding and management) second-stratum factor within the CHC model of intelligence.'

original_authors: Narayan, A.; Rivera, L.; Bernstein, R.; Harris, W.; Lieberman, A.
original_title: Positive childhood experiences predict less psychopathology and stress in pregnant women with childhood adversity: A pilot study of the benevolent childhood experiences (BCEs) scale
original_journal: Child Abuse & Neglect: The International Journal
description: Rates of total and individual Benevolent Childhood Experiences (BCEs) in a high-risk, low-income sample are similar across different high-risk populations (originally validated in low-income pregnant women with childhood adversity)
explanation: The authors hypothesized that BCEs frequencies would be similar to the pilot sample, and confirmed this: 'The mean number of BCEs in the two samples did not differ, t(147) = .74, ns,' with item-level frequencies differing significantly on only one of ten items. The authors state that 'mean levels of total BCEs and item frequencies were strikingly similar to the pilot sample.'

original_authors: Narayan, A.; Rivera, L.; Bernstein, R.; Harris, W.; Lieberman, A.
original_title: Positive childhood experiences predict less psychopathology and stress in pregnant women with childhood adversity: A pilot study of the benevolent childhood experiences (BCEs) scale
original_journal: Child Abuse & Neglect: The International Journal
description: Higher levels of Benevolent Childhood Experiences (BCEs) predict lower levels of psychological distress/mental health symptoms in high-risk adults, even after accounting for Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs)
explanation: The replication found that higher BCEs significantly predicted lower odds of psychological distress (β = −.35, p < .05, odds ratio = .71), consistent with the pilot study finding that higher BCEs predicted lower PTSD symptoms after accounting for ACEs. The authors state this is 'aligned with pilot findings that higher levels of BCEs were significantly correlated with lower levels of depression symptoms and perceived stress at the bivariate level.'

original_authors: Narayan, A.; Rivera, L.; Bernstein, R.; Harris, W.; Lieberman, A.
original_title: Positive childhood experiences predict less psychopathology and stress in pregnant women with childhood adversity: A pilot study of the benevolent childhood experiences (BCEs) scale
original_journal: Child Abuse & Neglect: The International Journal
description: Higher levels of Benevolent Childhood Experiences (BCEs) predict fewer stressful life events and lower contextual stress in high-risk adults, even after accounting for Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs)
explanation: The current study found that BCEs were not significantly correlated with sociodemographic risk (r = -.08, ns) or parenting stress (r = -.01, ns), and the planned regressions were not conducted because of these null bivariate associations. This fails to replicate the pilot finding that higher BCEs predicted fewer stressful life events. The authors explicitly acknowledge the discrepancy: 'BCEs were related to stressful life events in the pilot study but not to contextual stress in the current sample,' attributing it to different operationalizations of stress (trauma-specific events in the pilot vs. sociodemographic stressors in the current study). The parenting stress null should also be interpreted cautiously due to low internal consistency of the Parental Stress Scale (α = .66) and small sample size (N = 50).

original_authors: Kwapil, T.; Barrantes-Vidal, N.; Silvia, P.
original_title: The dimensional structure of the Wisconsin Schizotypy Scales: Factor identification and construct validity
description: Positive and negative schizotypy (assessed with the Wisconsin Schizotypy Scales) are associated with differential patterns of interview-assessed psychopathology, personality disorder traits, and impaired functioning in nonclinically ascertained young adults
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'Overall, the present study successfully replicated results from five prominent interview studies assessing the expression of multidimensional schizotypy in ostensibly high-functioning student samples,' with Study 1 (Kwapil et al., 2008) being one of the five. The current study used the MSS rather than the Wisconsin Schizotypy Scales, and added disorganized schizotypy, making this a close replication.

original_authors: Barrantes-Vidal, N.; Gross, G.; Sheinbaum, T.; Mitjavila, M.; Ballespí, S.; Kwapil, T.
original_title: Positive and negative schizotypy are associated with prodromal and schizophrenia-spectrum symptoms
description: Positive and negative schizotypy (assessed with the Wisconsin Schizotypy Scales) are associated with differential patterns of prodromal symptoms and schizophrenia-spectrum personality disorder traits in nonclinically ascertained young adults
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'successfully replicated findings from five previous schizotypy interview studies,' with Barrantes-Vidal et al. (2013) being one of the five. The current study used the MSS rather than the Wisconsin Schizotypy Scales, and added disorganized schizotypy, constituting a close replication.

original_authors: Kwapil, T.; Gross, G.; Silvia, P.; Barrantes-Vidal, N.
original_title: Prediction of psychopathology and functional impairment by positive and negative schizotypy in the Chapmans' ten-year longitudinal study
description: Positive and negative schizotypy (assessed with the Wisconsin Schizotypy Scales) predict differential patterns of interview-assessed psychopathology, personality disorder traits, and functional impairment in a 10-year longitudinal study
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'successfully replicated findings from five prominent interview studies,' with Kwapil et al. (2013) being Study 3 in their comparative Table 3. The current study used the MSS rather than the Wisconsin Schizotypy Scales and was cross-sectional rather than longitudinal, making this a close replication.

original_authors: Kemp, K.; Bathery, A.; Barrantes-Vidal, N.; Kwapil, T.
original_title: Positive, negative, and disorganized schizotypy predict differential patterns of interview-rated schizophrenia-spectrum symptoms and impairment
description: Positive, negative, and disorganized schizotypy (assessed with the Multidimensional Schizotypy Scale) are each associated with distinct patterns of interview-assessed schizophrenia-spectrum symptoms and functional impairment in nonclinically ascertained young adults
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'successfully replicated findings from five prominent interview studies,' with Kemp et al. (2021) as Study 4. This is the most methodologically similar prior study (both use the MSS), and the current study followed the same analytic procedures; the replication used a similar nonclinical student sample with the same predictor and outcome measures.

original_authors: Kwapil, T.; Clark, H.; Rbeiz, K.; Bathery, A.; Kemp, K.; Barrantes-Vidal, N.
original_title: Association of positive, negative, and disorganized schizotypy with cluster A, borderline, and avoidant personality disorders and traits
original_journal: Personality Disorders: Theory, Research, and Treatment
description: Positive, negative, and disorganized schizotypy (assessed with the Multidimensional Schizotypy Scale) are associated with distinct patterns of Cluster A, borderline, and avoidant personality disorder traits in nonclinically ascertained young adults
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'successfully replicated findings from five prominent interview studies,' with Kwapil et al. (2022) as Study 5. Both studies used the MSS and followed the same analytic procedures; the current study confirmed the pattern of associations between schizotypy dimensions and personality disorder traits reported in this study.

original_authors: Breland, J.; Donalson, R.; Li, Y.; Hebenstreit, C.; Goldstein, L.; Maguen, S.
original_title: Military sexual trauma is associated with eating disorders, while combat exposure is not
original_journal: Psychological Trauma: Theory, Research, Practice and Policy
description: Military sexual trauma (but not combat exposure) is an independent predictor of eating disorder pathology in female veterans when both trauma types are included in the same statistical model
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'our findings both replicate and extend those of Breland et al.' Using the same measures (LEC-5, EDDS-5) and same logistic regression approach in a markedly different population (food insecure community members vs. female veterans), sexual trauma was again the only significant predictor of eating disorder pathology (OR = 2.64; 95% CI [1.22, 5.71]), while combat exposure was not significant.

original_authors: Wtccc
original_title: Association study of 14 500 nsSNPs in four common diseases identifies variants involved in autoimmunity
description: Nine novel nonsynonymous SNP regions outside the HLA region are associated with Graves' disease at a point-wise significance level of P ≤ 10⁻⁴ in a genome-wide nsSNP scan of 900 GD cases and 1500 controls
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'we have failed to replicate, in an adequately powered independent data set, association of nine novel nsSNPs previously reported to be weakly associated with GD in the WTCCC nsSNP study.' None of the nine candidate nsSNPs showed association with GD in the independent replication (P = 0.215–0.841).

original_authors: Trynka, G.; Hunt, K.; Bockett, N.
original_title: Dense genotyping identifies and localizes multiple common and rare variant association signals in celiac disease
description: Multiple common and rare genetic variants (39 non-HLA loci plus the HLA locus) are associated with coeliac disease risk in European populations
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as 'the first replication study of CeD variants in a non-European population', directly testing Trynka et al. (2011)'s findings in north Indians. Only 5 of 44 tested non-HLA SNPs were directly replicated (p<0.05), with 2 additional loci confirmed via transferability analysis, while the HLA locus was strongly confirmed (p=8.17×10⁻⁴⁹); the authors attribute limited replication to modest sample size and insufficient power rather than absence of true effects.

original_authors: Hafler, D.; Compston, A.; Sawcer, S.; Lander, E.; Daly, M.; Jager, D.
original_title: Risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genomewide study
description: KIAA0350 (rs6498169) variant is associated with susceptibility to multiple sclerosis
explanation: The authors successfully replicated the KIAA0350 association in an Australian sample (P=0.001; OR 1.23), and when combined with IMSGC data, this reached genome-wide significance (P=3×10⁻⁸). They explicitly state: 'We replicated associations for four of the six top IMSGC candidate genes.'

original_authors: Hafler, D.; Compston, A.; Sawcer, S.; Lander, E.; Daly, M.; Jager, D.
original_title: Risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genomewide study
description: IL2RA (rs2104286) variant is associated with predisposition to multiple sclerosis
explanation: The IL2RA SNP rs2104286 was significantly associated with MS in the Australian sample (P=0.033; OR 1.16). The authors explicitly included IL2RA among the four replicated genes from the IMSGC GWAS.

original_authors: Hafler, D.; Compston, A.; Sawcer, S.; Lander, E.; Daly, M.; Jager, D.
original_title: Risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genomewide study
description: RPL5 (rs6604026) variant is associated with risk of multiple sclerosis
explanation: The RPL5 SNP rs6604026 was significantly associated with MS risk in the Australian sample (P=0.041; OR 1.14), and RPL5 is listed among the four genes the authors explicitly state were replicated from the IMSGC study.

original_authors: Hafler, D.; Compston, A.; Sawcer, S.; Lander, E.; Daly, M.; Jager, D.
original_title: Risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genomewide study
description: CD58 (rs12044852) variant is associated with susceptibility to multiple sclerosis
explanation: The CD58 SNP rs12044852 was significantly associated with MS susceptibility in the Australian sample (P=0.042; OR 1.2), and CD58 is listed among the four replicated genes from the IMSGC study.

original_authors: Hafler, D.; Compston, A.; Sawcer, S.; Lander, E.; Daly, M.; Jager, D.
original_title: Risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genomewide study
description: IL7R (rs6897932) variant is associated with risk of multiple sclerosis
explanation: The IL7R SNP rs6897932 showed no association with MS risk in the Australian sample (P=0.58). The authors note this as 'a notable exclusion from the list of replicated loci,' and the risk allele was actually slightly less frequent in cases than controls.

original_authors: Graham, D.; Graham, R.; Manku, H.; Wong, A.; Whittaker, J.; Gaffney, P.
original_title: Polymorphism at the TNF superfamily gene TNFSF4 confers susceptibility to systemic lupus erythematosus
description: TNFSF4 haplotypes in the upstream region of the gene are associated with risk for (and protection from) systemic lupus erythematosus
explanation: The authors explicitly confirm the association in three of four independent European cohorts and state in the abstract: 'This is the first replication study that confirms the association of genetic variation in the upstream region of TNFSF4 with susceptibility to SLE.' The risk haplotype (tagged by rs1234317 and rs12039904) was replicated with pooled OR=1.39 (p=0.0009) and OR=1.38 (p=0.0012), respectively.

original_authors: Hafler, D.; Compston, A.; Sawcer, S.; Lander, E.; Daly, M.
original_title: International multiple sclerosis genetics consortium. risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genome-wide study
original_journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
description: SNPs in candidate genes (CD6, CLEC16a, EVI5, GPC5, RGS1, TYK2, and others) are associated with multiple sclerosis risk in white populations of European ancestry
explanation: The paper tested 19 SNPs from 12 candidate MS genes in African Americans, explicitly calling it 'a replication of previously validated findings.' Results were mixed: 5 of 12 genes (CD6, CLEC16a, EVI5, GPC5, TYK2) 'convincingly replicated' while 7 (CD226, CD58, IL7R, IL2R, IRF8, RGS1, TNFRSF1A) failed to reach significance. However, the Cochrane heterogeneity Q test showed no significant differences between populations for any SNP, and authors note non-significant results may reflect lower statistical power (lower MAFs in African Americans) rather than true non-replication. The authors conclude the data is 'consistent with shared disease genetic mechanisms' across ancestries, but the partial pattern of significance warrants an inconclusive classification. PDF review confirmed these findings.

original_authors: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium
original_title: Genome-wide association study of 14,000 cases of seven common diseases and 3000 shared controls
description: Six single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) identified in a genome-wide association study are associated with essential hypertension in a European population
explanation: The authors conducted a replication study of the six WTCCC hypertension-associated SNPs in 7551 Korean individuals. They found no significant associations in the primary case-control analysis, and the Discussion notes 'inconsistent results across the three studies suggest that the complex nature of the genetic architecture affects the development of essential hypertension,' implying the original findings did not replicate. Only subgroup and quantitative trait associations were found, and none survived Bonferroni correction.

original_authors: Sethi, A.; Nordestgaard, B.; Tybjaerg-Hansen, A.
original_title: Angiotensinogen gene polymorphism, plasma angiotensinogen, and risk of hypertension and ischemic heart disease: a metaanalysis
description: The AGT rs699 (M235T) polymorphism in the angiotensinogen gene is associated with elevated blood pressure and increased risk of hypertension
explanation: The authors explicitly describe replicating the AGT rs699 association in a large Japanese sample. Results were significant for SBP (P=0.002), DBP (P=0.001), and in the joint meta-analysis the hypertension association reached genome-wide significance (P=7.3×10⁻¹⁰), which the Discussion describes as 'consistently replicated.'

original_authors: Sookoian, S.; Gianotti, T.; González, C.; Pirola, C.
original_title: Association of the C-344T aldosterone synthase gene variant with essential hypertension: a meta-analysis
description: The CYP11B2 rs1799998 (C-344T) aldosterone synthase gene variant is associated with essential hypertension, with the CC genotype being protective compared to TT
explanation: The CYP11B2 rs1799998 variant showed the most significant association with all three BP traits in the Japanese sample (SBP P=1.5×10⁻⁵, DBP P=1.8×10⁻⁵, hypertension OR=1.15, P=2.3×10⁻⁵), and hypertension association reached genome-wide significance (P=3.9×10⁻⁸) in the joint meta-analysis, which the authors describe as 'consistently replicated.'

original_authors: Staessen, J.; Wang, J.; Ginocchio, G.; Petrov, V.; Saavedra, A.; Soubrier, F.; Vlietinck, R.; Fagard, R.
original_title: The deletion/insertion polymorphism of the angiotensin converting enzyme gene and cardiovascular-renal risk
description: The ACE deletion/insertion (D/I) polymorphism (rs4340) is associated with blood pressure and risk of hypertension
explanation: Reviewed Table 2 from the PDF: ACE rs4341 showed no significant associations in the combined Japanese sample (SBP P=0.288, DBP P=0.199, hypertension OR=1.05 [0.98-1.12], P=0.145). It was significant only in CAGE panel 3 (not panels 1 or 2). The joint meta-analysis found a 'suggestive association' with hypertension (P=1.4×10⁻⁵) but with significant heterogeneity (P_hetero=0.019). The Discussion explicitly calls this 'suggestive' rather than a confirmed replication, warranting an inconclusive classification.

original_authors: Niu, W.; Zhang, Y.; Ji, K.; Gao, P.; Zhu, D.
original_title: Lack of association between alpha-adducin G460W polymorphism and hypertension: evidence from a case-control study and a meta-analysis
description: The ADD1 rs4961 (G460W) alpha-adducin gene polymorphism is associated with blood pressure and hypertension risk
explanation: Reviewed Table 2 from the PDF: ADD1 rs4961 showed clearly null results across all three BP traits in the Japanese sample — SBP beta=0.05 mmHg (P=0.789), DBP beta=0.13 mmHg (P=0.258), hypertension OR=0.99 [0.93-1.05] (P=0.805). The prior meta-analysis by Niu et al. itself reported 'lack of association,' and the present study likewise found no evidence of association, confirming failure to replicate the originally claimed ADD1-hypertension link. Figure 2 forest plot shows the combined OR centered on 1.0.

original_authors: Lou, Y.; Liu, J.; Huang, Y.; Liu, J.; Wang, Z.; Liu, Y.; Li, Z.; Li, Y.; Xie, Y.; Wen, S.
original_title: A46G and C79G polymorphisms in the b2-adrenergic receptor gene (ADRB2) and essential hypertension risk: a meta-analysis
description: The ADRB2 rs1042713 (R16G) polymorphism in the beta-2 adrenergic receptor gene is associated with essential hypertension risk
explanation: Reviewed Table 2 from the PDF: ADRB2 rs1042713 showed no significant associations in the combined Japanese sample — SBP beta=0.07 mmHg (P=0.708), DBP beta=0.14 mmHg (P=0.235), hypertension OR=1.06 [1.00-1.13] (P=0.071). The variant was significant only in CAGE panel 3, but not replicable in panels 1 and 2 (noted in Results). Inter-panel heterogeneity was significant for SBP (P_het=0.009) and DBP (P_het=0.012), indicating inconsistent effects. The Discussion does not identify ADRB2 as a confirmed replication.

original_authors: Bagos, P.; Elefsinioti, A.; Nikolopoulos, G.; Hamodrakas, S.
original_title: The GNB3 C825T polymorphism and essential hypertension: a meta-analysis of 34 studies including 14,094 cases and 17,760 controls
description: The GNB3 rs5443 (C825T) polymorphism in the G protein beta-3 subunit gene is associated with essential hypertension
explanation: Reviewed Table 2 from the PDF: GNB3 rs5443 showed no significant association and the direction was actually opposite to that expected — SBP beta=-0.32 mmHg (P=0.107), DBP beta=-0.19 mmHg (P=0.096), hypertension OR=0.97 [0.91-1.03] (P=0.340). The OR below 1.0 is in the opposite direction from a risk allele. The Discussion does not mention GNB3 as showing any positive replication. Figure 2 forest plot data was not available for GNB3 (as noted in figure caption), consistent with null results.

original_authors: Pereira, T.; Rudnicki, M.; Cheung, B.; Baum, L.; Yamada, Y.; Oliveira, P.; Pereira, A.; Krieger, J.
original_title: Three endothelial nitric oxide (NOS3) gene polymorphisms in hypertensive and normotensive individuals: meta-analysis of 53 studies reveals evidence of publication bias
description: The NOS3 rs1799983 (D298E) endothelial nitric oxide synthase gene polymorphism is associated with hypertension
explanation: Reviewed Table 2 from the PDF: NOS3 rs1799983 showed no significant associations in the Japanese sample — SBP beta=0.67 mmHg (P=0.071), DBP beta=0.32 mmHg (P=0.144), hypertension OR=1.03 [0.91-1.17] (P=0.615). The risk allele frequency is very low in this Japanese population (0.08), limiting power. The Discussion notes that a different NOS3 SNP (rs3918226) was found significant in Europeans but 'does not appear to be polymorphic in East Asians.' Figure 2 forest plot shows the combined NOS3 OR for hypertension centered near 1.0 across all studies.

original_authors: Lawford, B.; Young, R.; Swagell, C.; Barnes, M.; Burton, S.; Ward, W.
original_title: The C/C genotype of the C957T polymorphism of the dopamine D2 receptor is associated with schizophrenia
description: The C/C genotype of the DRD2 C957T (rs6277) polymorphism is associated with increased susceptibility to schizophrenia
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'We could replicate only rs6277 (corrected P-value of 0.014)' and that their results 'are consistent with the previous reports by other researchers on the positive association between the synonymous C957T (rs6277) polymorphism and schizophrenia, in different Caucasian populations,' successfully replicating the original finding in an independent Bulgarian sample.

original_authors: Hafler, D.; Compston, A.; Sawcer, S.; Lander, E.; Daly, M.; De Jager, P.
original_title: Risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genomewide study
description: 17 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 14 loci are associated with susceptibility to multiple sclerosis, with HLA-DRA and IL2RA reaching genome-wide significance
explanation: The paper explicitly attempts to replicate the 17 IMSGC SNPs in new Dutch and Canadian cohorts. Results are mixed: 5 SNPs (HLA-DRA, IL7R, IL2RA, CD58, CLEC16A) achieve genome-wide significance in the combined meta-analysis, while three loci (PDE4B, DBC1, ANKRD15) are suggested to be false positives and the majority of the other SNPs do not reach genome-wide significance. The authors confirm some associations but conclude that several previously reported associations were not replicated.

original_authors: Takahashi, Y.; Kou, I.; Takahashi, A.; Johnson, T.; Kono, K.; Kawakami, N.
original_title: A genome-wide association study identifies common variants near LBX1 associated with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
description: SNP rs11190870 near LBX1 is associated with susceptibility to adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) in Japanese females (GWAS finding with OR=1.56)
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'we successfully replicated the previous GWAS finding that rs11190870 was highly significantly associated with AIS' in an independent southern Chinese population, obtaining P=9.1×10⁻¹⁰ and OR=1.85 (95% CI 1.52-2.25). The replication extends the original Japanese GWAS finding to a different ethnic population using the same SNP association approach.

original_authors: Okamoto, K.; Iwasaki, N.; Nishimura, C.; Doi, K.; Noiri, E.; Nakamura, S.
original_title: Identification of KCNJ15 as a susceptibility gene in Asian patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
description: The T allele of rs3746876 within KCNJ15 is associated with increased risk of type 2 diabetes (especially in non-obese individuals) in Japanese populations
explanation: The authors explicitly state in their conclusion: 'the present study failed to validate the original finding; therefore, it is considered that the KCNJ15 locus still does not have a place on the list of confirmed type 2 diabetes susceptibility loci at this moment.' While rs3746876-T was significantly associated with type 2 diabetes in the replication, the direction of effect was opposite to the original (OR = 0.82, protective rather than risk-increasing), and a meta-analysis combining both studies was non-significant.

original_authors: Urabe, Y.; Tanikawa; Takahashi, A.; Okada, Y.; Morizono, T.; Tsunoda, T.
original_title: A genome-wide association study of nephrolithiasis in the Japanese population identifies novel susceptible loci at 5q35.3, 7p14.3, and 13q14.1
description: The SNP rs12654812 at the 5q35.3 locus (RGS14-SLC34A1-PFN3-F12 region) is associated with increased risk of nephrolithiasis in the Japanese population
explanation: The replication successfully confirmed the 5q35.3 locus association (rs12654812: P = 3.12 × 10⁻³, OR = 1.43) after Bonferroni correction in an independent Japanese cohort. The authors explicitly state 'we successfully validated three nephrolithiasis loci (5q35.5, 7p14.33 and 13q14.1) in an independent cohort.'

original_authors: Urabe, Y.; Tanikawa; Takahashi, A.; Okada, Y.; Morizono, T.; Tsunoda, T.
original_title: A genome-wide association study of nephrolithiasis in the Japanese population identifies novel susceptible loci at 5q35.3, 7p14.3, and 13q14.1
description: The SNP rs12669187 at the 7p14.3 locus (INMT-FAM188B-AQP1 region) is associated with increased risk of nephrolithiasis in the Japanese population
explanation: The replication successfully confirmed the 7p14.3 locus association (rs12669187: P = 6.43 × 10⁻³, OR = 1.57) after Bonferroni correction in an independent Japanese cohort. The authors explicitly state 'we successfully validated three nephrolithiasis loci' in their discussion.

original_authors: Urabe, Y.; Tanikawa; Takahashi, A.; Okada, Y.; Morizono, T.; Tsunoda, T.
original_title: A genome-wide association study of nephrolithiasis in the Japanese population identifies novel susceptible loci at 5q35.3, 7p14.3, and 13q14.1
description: The SNP rs7981733 at the 13q14.1 locus (DGKH gene region) is associated with increased risk of nephrolithiasis in the Japanese population
explanation: The replication successfully confirmed the 13q14.1 locus association (rs7981733: P = 5.00 × 10⁻³, OR = 1.41) after Bonferroni correction in an independent Japanese cohort. The authors explicitly state 'we successfully validated three nephrolithiasis loci' and note 'the three loci showed a stronger association (OR, 1.43, 1.57 and 1.41) than those reported in the previous GWAS.'

original_authors: De Boer, Y.; Van Gerven, N.; Zwiers, A.; Verwer, B.; Van Hoek, B.; Van Erpecum, K.
original_title: Genome-wide association study identifies variants associated with autoimmune hepatitis type 1
description: The G allele of SNP rs4325730, located upstream of the ICOS gene in the CD28/CTLA4/ICOS cluster at chromosome 2q33.2, is a genetic risk factor for type 1 autoimmune hepatitis in a European population
explanation: The authors explicitly describe their study as 'a replication study' of the original European GWAS, testing the same SNP (rs4325730) in a Japanese population. They found significant association (P = 0.0173, OR 1.30) and stated in the Discussion: 'we were the first to replicate the association of SNPs in non-HLA region reported in the genome-wide association study with Japanese AIH.'

original_authors: Chen, Z.; Tao, S.; Gao, Y.; Zhang, J.; Hu, Y.; Mo, L.
original_title: Genome-wide association study of sex hormones, gonadotropins and sex hormone-binding protein in Chinese men
description: The rs2414095 SNP in the CYP19A1 gene is significantly associated with circulating FSH levels in Chinese men
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'we successfully validated the results of the association of the rs2414095 SNP from the previous GWAS,' and the combined analysis in Japanese men yielded a highly significant association (β_STD = 0.15, P = 9.7 × 10⁻⁵), replicating the original finding in a new population.

original_authors: Rossille, D.; Gressier, M.; Damotte, D.; Maucort-Boulch, D.; Pangault, C.; Semana, G.
original_title: High level of soluble programmed cell death ligand 1 in blood impacts overall survival in aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: results from a French multicenter clinical trial
description: Elevated soluble PD-L1 (sPD-L1) in blood is associated with inferior overall survival in newly diagnosed DLBCL patients treated with rituximab-based chemotherapy
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'validated prior findings' and report the US cohort result 'replicated' the original French finding (HR=1.72; 95%CI 0.99-2.98 vs original HR=1.87; 95%CI 1.10-3.19), concluding 'pre-treatment soluble PD-L1 was confirmed to be an adverse prognostic factor.' The paper's own title describes it as a 'replication study.'

original_authors: Baum, A.E.; Akula, N.; Cabanero, M.; Cardona, I.; Corona, W.; Klemens, B. et al.
original_title: A genome-wide association study implicates diacylglycerol kinase eta (DGKH) and several other genes in the etiology of bipolar disorder
description: Three SNPs (rs9315885, rs1012053, rs1170191) in the first intron of DGKH (diacylglycerol kinase eta) are associated with bipolar disorder I at the single-marker level
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'Our study does not replicate the single-marker association reported by Baum et al.' None of the three SNPs showed significant association after permutation correction (all permutation p-values > 0.05), though a haplotype finding was noted as requiring cautious interpretation.

original_authors: Jabbi, M.; Korf, J.; Kema, I.P.; Hartman, C.A.; van der Pompe, G.; Minderaa, R.B.
original_title: Genetically based reduced MAOA and COMT functioning is associated with the cortisol stress response
description: COMT met/met genotype in combination with low MAOA expression (predominantly in males) is associated with increased hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis response (adrenocorticotropic hormone) to a social stressor
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'We replicated this association in adolescent boys with saliva cortisol,' confirming the COMT met/met + low MAOA interaction on HPA axis stress response. The replication used a different population (adolescents), a different stress paradigm (GSST), and a different biomarker (salivary cortisol vs. ACTH), but found the same directional effect specifically in males.

original_authors: Chen, G.; Kono, N.; Geschwind, D.; Cantor, R.
original_title: Quantitative trait locus analysis of nonverbal communication in autism spectrum disorder
description: A quantitative trait locus (QTL) analysis of nonverbal communication deficits in autism spectrum disorder identified five chromosomal loci, including a genome-wide significant locus on chromosome 1 (Z=3.6, P<0.0001), in 228 AGRE families
explanation: The authors explicitly conducted a direct replication of the chromosome-1 QTL in an independent sample of 213 AGRE families using the same NVC trait, same ADI-R instrument, same QTL analysis method, and overlapping marker set. They state: 'formal replication is only observed on chromosome 1p21.2-1p12, where the QTL from the prior and current study are coincident,' with a Z-score of 3.36 (P<0.0004) meeting the pre-specified replication criterion of Z>2.33.

original_authors: Zuo, L.; Kranzler, H.; Luo, X.; Covault, J.; Gelernter, J.
original_title: CNR1 variation modulates risk for drug and alcohol dependence
description: Interaction between two independent CNR1 variants (SNP3^G+ and SNP8^T/T) significantly increases risk for drug dependence (including cocaine dependence) in European Americans
explanation: The present study explicitly calls itself a replication and finds that the CNR1 interaction replicates in European American samples (EA family sample P=0.015, EA case-control P=0.003) but fails to replicate in African American samples, yielding mixed results. The authors note 'the present study extended the initial study and had different study targets of interest,' as they test cocaine dependence specifically rather than the broad drug dependence phenotype examined in the original.

original_authors: Göpel, W.; Kim, D.; Gortner, L.
original_title: Prothrombotic mutations as a risk factor for preterm birth
description: Fetal Factor V Leiden (FVL) mutation (rs6025) is associated with increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth in Caucasians
explanation: The paper's title explicitly identifies this as 'a case-control replication study.' Table 3 shows fetal FVL significantly associated with PTB (OR: 2.6, 95% CI: 1.31-5.17, P = 0.008). The Discussion states: 'Our replication analysis supports the association of fetal FVL with PTB, and meta-analysis supports a positive association of fetal FVL with PTB.' Meta-analysis (Figure 1c) across 4 prior studies plus this one confirms the association (OR: 2.71, 95% CI: 1.15-6.40, P = 0.02). The original finding was reported across multiple prior studies (Göpel 1999, Resch 2004, Gibson 2007); Göpel 1999 was the earliest report.

original_authors: Menon, R.; Velez, D.; Thorsen, P.
original_title: Ethnic differences in key candidate genes for spontaneous preterm birth: TNF-alpha and its receptors
description: Fetal TNF-alpha 308 (rs1800629) polymorphism is associated with spontaneous preterm birth in Caucasians
explanation: Table 3 shows no significant association between fetal TNF-alpha 308 and PTB (OR: 0.89, 95% CI: 0.62-1.28, P = 0.52). Meta-analysis (Figure 1a) across 5 studies also found no significant association (OR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.65-1.03, P = 0.08, fixed effects, I²=0%). The previously reported positive association was clearly not replicated. Verified against PDF Table 3 and forest plot Figure 1a.

original_authors: Lorenz, E.; Hallman, M.; Marttila, R.; Haataja, R.; Schwartz, D.
original_title: Association between the Asp299Gly polymorphisms in the Toll-like receptor 4 and premature births in the Finnish population
description: Fetal TLR4 299 (rs4986790) polymorphism is associated with spontaneous preterm birth
explanation: Table 3 shows no significant association between fetal TLR4 299 and PTB (OR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.53-1.54, P = 0.92). Meta-analysis (Figure 1b) across 3 studies also found no significant association (OR: 1.07, 95% CI: 0.66-1.73, P = 0.78, random effects, I²=69%). The previously reported positive association was clearly not replicated. Verified against PDF Table 3 and forest plot Figure 1b.

original_authors: Simhan, H.; Krohn, M.; Roberts, J.; Zeevi, A.; Caritis, S.
original_title: Interleukin-6 promoter -174 polymorphism and spontaneous preterm birth
original_journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
description: Maternal IL-6 -174 (rs1800795) polymorphism is associated with spontaneous preterm birth
explanation: Table 3 shows no significant association between maternal IL-6 -174 and PTB (OR: 0.83, 95% CI: 0.64-1.06, P = 0.13). Meta-analysis (Figure 1d) across 3 studies also found no significant association (OR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.35-1.03, P = 0.07, random effects, I²=87%). The previously reported positive association was clearly not replicated. Verified against PDF Table 3 and forest plot Figure 1d.

original_authors: Gibson, C.; Maclennan, A.; Dekker, G.
original_title: Genetic polymorphisms and spontaneous preterm birth
description: Fetal PAI-2 (rs6103) polymorphism is associated with spontaneous preterm birth
explanation: Table 3 shows no significant association between fetal PAI-2 and PTB (OR: 0.51, 95% CI: 0.18-1.48, P = 0.18, recessive genetic model). No meta-analysis was conducted for this SNP due to insufficient prior studies. The previously reported positive association from Gibson et al. (2007) was clearly not replicated. Verified against PDF Table 3.

original_authors: Gibson, C.; Maclennan, A.; Dekker, G.
original_title: Genetic polymorphisms and spontaneous preterm birth
description: Fetal THBD (rs1800576) polymorphism is associated with spontaneous preterm birth
explanation: Table 3 shows OR: 0 (NA), P = 0.36, because zero cases carried the THBD AG genotype (0 of 169 cases vs 7 of 570 controls). The test was essentially uninformative due to the very low minor allele frequency, so confidence remains low — the replication could not meaningfully evaluate the original association. Verified against PDF Table 3; no meta-analysis was conducted for this SNP.

original_authors: Göpel, W.; Kim, D.; Gortner, L.
original_title: Prothrombotic mutations as a risk factor for preterm birth
description: Fetal prothrombin gene mutation (PGM, rs1799963) is associated with spontaneous preterm birth in Caucasians
explanation: Table 3 shows no significant association between fetal PGM and PTB (OR: 1.62, 95% CI: 0.65-4.05, P = 0.31). Meta-analysis (Figure 1e) across 4 studies also found no significant association (OR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.37-2.38, P = 0.89, random effects, I²=71%). The previously reported positive association was clearly not replicated. Verified against PDF Table 3 and forest plot Figure 1e.

original_authors: Gibson, C.; Maclennan, A.; Dekker, G.
original_title: Genetic polymorphisms and spontaneous preterm birth
description: Fetal ADD1 (rs4961) polymorphism is associated with spontaneous preterm birth
explanation: Table 3 shows no significant association between fetal ADD1 and PTB (OR: 0.98, 95% CI: 0.72-1.32, P = 0.87). No meta-analysis was conducted for this SNP due to insufficient prior studies. The previously reported positive association from Gibson et al. (2007) was clearly not replicated. Verified against PDF Table 3.

original_authors: Li, A.; Zalesky, A.; Yue, W.; Howes, O.; Yan, H.; Liu, Y.
original_title: A neuroimaging biomarker for striatal dysfunction in schizophrenia
description: A functional striatal abnormalities (FSA) index derived from resting-state fMRI can accurately discriminate individuals with non-affective psychosis from healthy controls with approximately 80% accuracy
explanation: The authors explicitly conclude that 'the original findings on the performance of the FSA as a diagnostic biomarker for schizophrenia are generalizable out of sample,' with AUC = 75.7% replicating the original 80.1%, and consistently higher FSA values in controls than patients, better non-affective classification, and GSR benefits all consistent with the original.

original_authors: Li, A.; Zalesky, A.; Yue, W.; Howes, O.; Yan, H.; Liu, Y.
original_title: A neuroimaging biomarker for striatal dysfunction in schizophrenia
description: Baseline FSA scores significantly correlate with symptom improvement following antipsychotic treatment (r = 0.62 and r = 0.42, both p < 0.01 in two cohorts), indicating FSA has prognostic capability
explanation: The replication found near-zero correlations between baseline FSA and symptom improvement (r = 0.038-0.089, p = 0.45-0.75), and the authors explicitly conclude that 'the original correlation between baseline FSA and treatment response did not replicate, and therefore it cannot be confirmed that the FSA has external validity as a prognostic biomarker.'

original_authors: Tong, B.; Jutzeler, C.; Cragg, J.; Grassner, L.; Schwab, J.; Casha, S.
original_title: Serum albumin predicts long-term neurological outcomes after acute spinal cord injury
description: Serum albumin concentrations measured early after spinal cord injury (within 1 month) are associated with baseline injury severity and independently predict long-term neurological outcomes after adjustment for baseline injury characteristics
explanation: The authors describe their results as 'partially confirm[ing] our previous observations.' The current study replicated the finding that serum albumin associates with baseline injury severity, and found unadjusted associations with 1-year outcomes, but failed to replicate the key finding that serum albumin independently predicts neurological recovery after adjusting for baseline injury severity. The replication used a different contemporary dataset (SCIRehab vs. Sygen trial), different albumin measurement timing, and a different statistical approach (URP-CTREE vs. linear/logistic regression).

original_authors: Orekhova, E.
original_title: EEG hyper-connectivity in high-risk infants is associated with later autism
description: Higher global alpha EEG connectivity (7-8 Hz) at 14 months of age in high-risk infants predicts later ASD diagnosis at 36 months
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'we did not replicate the previous observation of elevated connectivity in high-risk infants with later ASD.' No significant differences in global or network-level alpha connectivity were found between the HR-ASD group and comparison groups.

original_authors: Orekhova, E.
original_title: EEG hyper-connectivity in high-risk infants is associated with later autism
description: Higher alpha EEG functional connectivity in fronto-central connections at 14 months associates with greater severity of restricted and repetitive behaviours (RRBs) measured by ADI-R at 36 months in infants with later ASD diagnosis
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'we replicate the finding of an association between elevated connectivity over fronto-central connections based on the previous study and later restrictive and repetitive behaviours in infants with later ASD.' The replication found a significant correlation between fronto-central connectivity and ADI-R RRB scores within the HR-ASD group (Spearman's rho = 0.60, p = 0.037).

original_authors: Whitfield-Gabrieli, S.
original_title: Brain connectomics predict response to treatment in social anxiety disorder
description: Baseline resting-state fMRI amygdala connectivity can predict response to cognitive-behavioral therapy for social anxiety disorder, with amygdala connectivity explaining 21% of the variance in treatment outcomes above and beyond baseline symptom severity
explanation: The replication found only 2% additional variance explained by amygdala connectivity (vs. 21% in the original), with marginal statistical significance (p = 0.097-0.101). The authors conclude: 'This model provided a small improvement in the prediction of treatment response... approximately 1/10th of the effect size in the original report,' and 'A more flexible test of model replication...found no significant prediction of treatment response.'

original_authors: Zheng, H.; Ford, B.; Bergamino, M.; Kuplicki, R.; Tulsa, I.; Hunt, P.
original_title: A hidden menace? Cytomegalovirus infection is associated with reduced cortical gray matter volume in major depressive disorder
description: HCMV seropositivity is associated with reduced gray matter volume in several brain regions (particularly orbitofrontal, temporal, and parietal areas) in individuals with major depressive disorder
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the conclusion: 'we replicate the finding that HCMV infection is associated with GMV reduction in the context of MDD.' Two specific regions (right lateral orbitofrontal cortex and left pars orbitalis) showed significant volume reduction in the HCMV+ group in both the original and replication studies, using an identical statistical procedure in a fully independent sample.

original_authors: Effron, D.; Raj, M.
original_title: Misinformation and morality: encountering fake-news headlines makes them seem less unethical to publish and share
description: Repeated exposure to false headlines reduces moral condemnation of sharing them (Study 4: participants who saw headlines in a familiarization stage rated those headlines as less unethical to share than novel headlines they had not previously seen)
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'We successfully replicated the finding that repeated exposure decreases moral condemnation.' The replication effect estimate (β = -4.66pp) was functionally identical to the original (β = -4.64pp), and the paper is described as a registered report with a 'clear conceptual replication of the negative effect of repetition on moral condemnation.'

original_authors: Louie, K.; Khaw, M.; Glimcher, P.
original_title: Normalization is a general neural mechanism for context-dependent decision making
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
description: Higher-value distractor options decrease relative choice accuracy between two target options in ternary food-snack choices, attributed to divisive normalization of neural value representations
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'we could not replicate the distractor effect' and describe 'our unsuccessful replication'. Using the Small Telescopes approach and a Bayes factor of BF01 = 241, they obtained very strong evidence for the null hypothesis, with an effect size of Cohen's d = -0.01 (95% CI = [-0.01, 0.01]) compared to the original's significant negative effect.

original_authors: Louie, K.; Khaw, M.; Glimcher, P.
original_title: Normalization is a general neural mechanism for context-dependent decision making
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
description: Higher-value distractor options decrease relative choice accuracy between two target options in ternary food-snack choices, attributed to divisive normalization of neural value representations
explanation: The eye-tracking experiment also failed to replicate the distractor effect on choice accuracy (d = 0.03, p = .583, one-sided). The authors conclude 'the results of our two studies and the reanalysis of a previously published dataset suggest that there is no reliable distractor effect on choices.' The eye-tracking design added additional features (triangular option layout, keyboard responses, eye-tracking) and is classified as a close extension.

original_authors: Cohn, A.; Fehr, E.; Maréchal, M.
original_title: Business culture and dishonesty in the banking industry
description: Bankers primed to think about their professional identity (compared to those primed about leisure activities) become more dishonest, as measured by over-reporting of winning coin flips in an incentivized task
explanation: The Asia Pacific banker study (n=620) found a very small, non-significant effect (Cohen's d=0.06, p=0.111) compared to the original's d=0.37, p=0.017. The authors explicitly state: 'we do not find any significant increase in dishonesty among primed bankers in the Middle East and Asia Pacific, in contrast to the main study of the original publication.'

original_authors: Cohn, A.; Fehr, E.; Maréchal, M.
original_title: Business culture and dishonesty in the banking industry
description: Bankers primed to think about their professional identity (compared to those primed about leisure activities) become more dishonest, as measured by over-reporting of winning coin flips in an incentivized task
explanation: The Middle East banker study (n=148) found a very small, non-significant effect (Cohen's d=0.11, p=0.261). The authors conclude that 'the findings of the original main study did not replicate based on the conventional significance level of α=0.05 in the...Middle Eastern...individual banker samples.'

original_authors: Gudbjartsson, D.
original_title: A sequence variant in ZFHX3 on 16q22 associates with atrial fibrillation and ischemic stroke
description: A sequence variant (rs7193343) in ZFHX3 on chromosome 16q22 is associated with ischemic stroke (particularly cardioembolic stroke)
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'replicated 16q22 (ZFHX3) as a risk locus for CE (OR = 1.62 for the T allele; 95% CI, 1.26–2.07, p = 0.0014) and found this locus significantly associated with overall IS (OR = 1.28; 95% CI, 1.12–1.47, p = 0.002)', confirming the original association in a Dutch population.

original_authors: Kilarski, L.
original_title: Meta-analysis in more than 17,900 cases of ischemic stroke reveals a novel association at 12q24.12
description: Variant rs2634074 at the PITX2 locus (4q25) is associated with cardioembolic ischemic stroke
explanation: The authors 'confirmed the association at rs2634074 with CE stroke (OR = 1.43 for the T allele; 95% CI, 1.13–1.81, p = 0.029)' in a Dutch population, successfully replicating the previously reported association.

original_authors: Gretarsdottir, S.
original_title: Risk variants for atrial fibrillation on chromosome 4q25 associate with ischemic stroke
description: Variant rs2200733 at the PITX2 locus (4q25) is associated with cardioembolic ischemic stroke
explanation: The authors could not replicate the association at rs2200733 (OR = 1.30; 95% CI, 0.96–1.76; p = 0.60), reporting in the Discussion that this failure was likely due to limited power (56%) owing to the lower frequency of this variant.

original_authors: Ninds Stroke G.; Network (Sign); Isgc I.
original_title: Loci associated with ischaemic stroke and its subtypes (SiGN): a genome-wide association study
description: Variant rs12122341 at the TSPAN2 locus (1p13.2) is associated with large artery atherosclerotic ischemic stroke
explanation: The authors 'could not replicate the previously-established associations at the 1p13.2 (TSPAN2)' locus; the replication OR was 1.09 (95% CI, 0.90–1.32, p = 0.99) in the Dutch population.

original_authors: Holliday, E.
original_title: Common variants at 6p21.1 are associated with large artery atherosclerotic stroke
description: Variant rs556621 at the SUPT3H/CDC5L locus (6p21.1) is associated with large artery atherosclerotic stroke
explanation: The authors could not replicate the association at 6p21.1 (SUPT3H/CDC5L); OR was 0.89 (95% CI, 0.44–1.06, p = 0.86) and notably the effect direction was reversed relative to the original report.

original_authors: Bellenguez, C.
original_title: Genome-wide association study identifies a variant in HDAC9 associated with large vessel ischemic stroke
description: Variant rs2107595 at the HDAC9 locus (7p21.1) is associated with large vessel ischemic stroke
explanation: The authors could not replicate the association at 7p21.1 (HDAC9); the replication OR for rs2107595 was 1.22 (95% CI, 0.99–1.51, p = 0.43), not reaching significance in the Dutch population.

original_authors: Gschwendtner, A.
original_title: Sequence variants on chromosome 9p21.3 confer risk for atherosclerotic stroke
description: Variant rs2383207 at the CDKN2B-AS1 locus (9p21.3) is associated with atherosclerotic stroke
explanation: The authors could not replicate the 9p21.3 (CDKN2B-AS1) association; OR was 1.24 (95% CI, 1.05–1.46) for LAA but p = 0.11, which did not reach significance, and the authors listed it as a failed replication.

original_authors: Williams, F.
original_title: Ischemic stroke is associated with the ABO locus: the EuroCLOT study
description: Variant rs505922 at the ABO locus (9q34) is associated with ischemic stroke
explanation: The authors could not replicate the ABO (9q34) association; OR for overall IS was 1.09 (95% CI, 0.97–1.22, p = 0.74), not reaching significance, and it was listed among the failed replications in the Discussion.

original_authors: Kilarski, L.
original_title: Meta-analysis in more than 17,900 cases of ischemic stroke reveals a novel association at 12q24.12
description: Variant rs10744777 at the ALDH2 locus (12q24) is associated with ischemic stroke
explanation: The authors could not replicate the 12q24 (ALDH2) association; OR for overall IS was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.90–1.12, p = 1.00), and it was listed among the failed replications in the Discussion.

original_authors: Senapati, S.
original_title: Genome-wide analysis of methotrexate pharmacogenomics in rheumatoid arthritis shows multiple novel risk variants and leads for TYMS regulation
description: Eleven SNPs identified by genome-wide association study (GWAS) are associated with response to methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis patients
explanation: None of the 11 SNPs selected from this GWAS reached the authors' pre-specified Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold in the replication cohort of 915 patients; the authors conclude that 'it is not surprising that we did not replicate any of the SNPs selected from that GWAS in our study.'

original_authors: Chen, Y.; Zou, K.; Sun, J.; Yang, Y.; Liu, G.
original_title: Are gene polymorphisms related to treatment outcomes of methotrexate in patients with rheumatoid arthritis? A systematic review and meta-analysis
description: Fourteen SNPs from candidate gene studies (including rs1801394 in MTRR) are associated with response to methotrexate in patients with rheumatoid arthritis
explanation: Of the 14 candidate gene SNPs tested, only 1 (rs1801394 in MTRR) survived Bonferroni correction (ΔDAS28 β=−0.14, SE=0.04, p=0.0016; EULAR NR OR=1.39, 95% CI 1.11–1.75, p=0.004), while the remaining 13 SNPs failed to replicate. Three of the four SNPs showing nominal association were in the opposite direction to prior reports. The authors conclude 'this lack of reproducibility is common for candidate gene studies' but highlight rs1801394 as robustly replicated. Classified as inconclusive because the aggregate result is mixed: 1 of 14 SNPs replicated convincingly, but the vast majority failed. The original study cited is the systematic review that guided SNP selection; the 14 SNPs came from multiple primary studies (refs 7–21).

original_authors: Chen, Q.
original_title: Automated drusen segmentation and quantification in SD-OCT images
description: An algorithm for automated drusen segmentation and quantification in SD-OCT images achieves high accuracy (overlap ratio 67-76%) on OCT image data
