explanation: The authors re-implemented Chen et al.'s algorithm and tested it on an independent dataset using the same metrics, finding substantially lower performance (overlap ratio 25-39% vs. 67-76% originally reported). They conclude: 'we replicated a reportedly well-performing algorithm for OCT-based drusen quantification and found algorithm performance to be inferior to the reported results.'

original_authors: Volz, K.; Vogeley, K.; Tittgemeyer, M.; Von Cramon, D.; Sutter, M.
original_title: The neural basis of deception in strategic interactions
description: Deceptive intentions (both telling false statements and manipulative truth-telling) compared to truth-telling are associated with increased BOLD signals in the right temporoparietal junction (rTPJ), a region involved in socio-cognitive/Theory of Mind processes, during a strategic sender-receiver game
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the conclusion: 'The obtained results not only replicate but also expand the results of Volz et al. (2015)'; and in the Discussion: 'This result replicates the findings of Volz and colleagues regarding the involvement of the rTPJ in actions with deceptive intentions.' The same sender-receiver game paradigm was used but translated to Russian and run in Russia with Russian-speaking participants.

original_authors: Laukkonen, R.; Kaveladze, B.; Tangen, J.; Schooler, J.
original_title: The dark side of Eureka: Artificially induced aha moments make facts feel true
description: Artificially induced aha moments (from solving anagrams) increase the perceived truth of mundane facts presented simultaneously, due to misattribution of the feeling of insight
explanation: The paper explicitly tests and extends the 'insight misattribution' effect from Laukkonen et al. (2020) — which demonstrated the effect with mundane facts — to worldview beliefs, using the same anagram paradigm. Both the demonstration and internal replication samples confirmed the effect, with the Discussion concluding that 'artificially induced aha experiences can impact people's assessments of central premises about the world.'

original_authors: Tang, C.
original_title: Differential diagnosis of parkinsonism: A metabolic imaging study using pattern analysis
description: An FDG-PET automated probabilistic two-level classification algorithm can accurately differentiate between Parkinson's disease (PD) and atypical parkinsonian syndromes (APS) using disease-specific metabolic brain patterns
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion that the FDG-PET automated classification algorithm 'has been replicated in 35 Swedish patients with PD, MSA and PSP with very good accuracy,' achieving 84% sensitivity and 100% specificity for PD vs. APS at level 1, consistent with pooled meta-analysis results (sensitivity 0.84, specificity 0.96). The replication applied the same algorithm with the same cut-off values to a new geographic cohort (Stockholm, Sweden).

original_authors: Guevarra, D.; Moser, J.; Wager, T.; Kross, E.
original_title: Placebos without deception reduce self-report and neural measures of emotional distress
description: An open-label placebo (OLP) administered via saline nasal spray reduces emotional distress and late positive potential (LPP) amplitudes while viewing unpleasant scenes
explanation: The authors explicitly state their study aimed at 'a conceptual replication' of Guevarra et al. and conclude that findings were 'consistent with a previous OLP/EEG study,' demonstrating that OLP reduced both subjective distress (less arousal, lower anger intensity ratings) and LPP amplitudes. The study used facial expressions rather than unpleasant scenes, making it a conceptual rather than direct replication.

original_authors: Ishihara, M.; Keller, P.; Rossetti, Y.; Prinz, W.
original_title: Horizontal spatial representations of time: evidence for the STEARC effect
description: Participants show faster left-hand responses to auditory targets with early onset timing and faster right-hand responses to targets with late onset timing (the STEARC effect), when judging onset timing of an auditory target relative to a reference beat sequence
explanation: The authors explicitly describe Experiment 1 as 'a conceptual replication of the original study' and state in the Conclusion: 'Consistently with the original work by Ishihara et al., we successfully replicated the STEARC effect by employing a direct task in Experiment 1.' The key methodological difference was using four onset timing conditions (two early, two late) instead of the original two.

original_authors: Roozenbeek, J.; Van Der Linden, S.
original_title: Breaking harmony square: A game that "inoculates" against political misinformation
original_journal: Harvard Kennedy School HKS Misinformation Review
description: Playing the Harmony Square game inoculates players against political misinformation, reducing perceived reliability and sharing intentions of manipulative content, and increasing confidence in detecting manipulation techniques
explanation: The replication using a different game (Cat Park) successfully replicated two of three hypotheses: participants found misinformation less reliable (d = 0.95, p < 0.001) and were less willing to share it (d = 0.54, p < 0.001), but unlike the original Harmony Square study, Cat Park players did not become significantly more confident in their ability to identify misinformation (p = 0.204, d = -0.13). The authors themselves describe it as 'a mostly successful conceptual replication.'

original_authors: Szekely, A.
original_title: Evidence from a long-term experiment that collective risks change social norms and promote cooperation
description: Different behavioural types (empirical cooperators, normative cooperators, social norm followers, threshold-driven types, and unconditional types) emerge in a collective-risk social dilemma experiment and respond differently to empirical and normative expectations
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'Wave 2 convincingly replicated the existence of behavioural types. Not only can participants be classified in the same groups, but even the percentage of each type in the population is approximately the same.' The same five behavioral types were identified in Wave 2 in similar proportions.

original_authors: Szekely, A.
original_title: Evidence from a long-term experiment that collective risks change social norms and promote cooperation
description: Strong social norms that emerge under high risk make cooperative behaviour 'sticky', creating inertia so that cooperation decreases more slowly after a decrease in risk than it increases after a risk increase
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'Unexpectedly, we do not replicate the resilience of cooperative behaviour when moving from High to Low risk.' In Wave 2, contributions in the High Low treatment dropped immediately and significantly when risk changed (b = -4.833, p < 0.001), unlike Wave 1 where norms created an inertia effect.

original_authors: Hopkins, A.; Dolan, R.; Button, K.; Moutoussis, M.
original_title: A reduced self-positive belief underpins greater sensitivity to negative evaluation in socially anxious individuals
description: In social evaluation learning, a reduced positive self-belief (rather than biased updating or learning rates) is the primary computational mechanism underpinning greater sensitivity to negative social feedback in socially anxious individuals, and belief updating models outperform associative learning models in explaining this
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'these results replicate our previous analyses [34]' (p.7). Two authors (Moutoussis, Button) overlap with the original study, confirming this is a self-replication. The core finding from Hopkins et al. (2021) — that reduced positive self-beliefs about the self (b_Self), rather than biased updating or learning rates, is the primary computational mechanism in social anxiety — replicated significantly in both the mega-analysis (β = −0.18, p < .001) and the independent pre-registered dataset (β = −0.10, p = .013). Belief updating models also outperformed associative learning models across both datasets. The one finding that did NOT replicate was the secondary association between slower belief updating (λ) and depression (Mega-analysis: β = −0.15, p = .002; Preregistered: β = −0.04, p = .251). Overall the paper's primary replication target — the role of reduced positive self-beliefs — was clearly successful.

original_authors: Kesselmeier, M.
original_title: High-throughput DNA methylation analysis in anorexia nervosa confirms TNXB hypermethylation
description: Hypomethylation at the NR1H3 gene locus in females with anorexia nervosa compared to healthy-lean controls, as identified by epigenome-wide association study (EWAS) of whole blood DNA methylation
explanation: The authors explicitly aimed to replicate their own previous finding of hypomethylation at NR1H3 in AN using a larger independent sample, and clearly report failure: 'we were unable to replicate methylation differences at NR1H3, regardless of the methylation direction previously reported.' Despite including 189 AN patients and 67 controls, no significant methylation differences were found at any of the 15 investigated CpG sites.

original_authors: Wang, S.; Itthipuripat, S.; Ku, Y.
original_title: Electrical stimulation over human posterior parietal cortex selectively enhances the capacity of visual short-term memory
description: Anodal tDCS over the right posterior parietal cortex (PPC), but not the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), selectively improves visual working memory capacity (but not precision) especially at high memory load (set size 6)
explanation: The authors explicitly call this a 'conceptual replication' and clearly reject their main hypothesis: 'we found no credible evidence of such selective effects' and 'our Hypothesis 1 (improvements of capacity) was rejected.' The absence of the PPC-tDCS effect was supported by strong Bayesian evidence (BF+0_10 = 1/20.20).

original_authors: Thibodeau, P.; Boroditsky, L.
original_title: Metaphors we think with: The role of metaphor in reasoning
description: The metaphor used to describe a city's crime problem (beast vs. virus) influences the type of counter-measures participants suggest, with beast framing eliciting enforcement proposals and virus framing eliciting reform proposals
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'our results represent a successful replication of the metaphor-framing effect reported by Thibodeau and Boroditsky' and conclude 'the successful replication of Thibodeau and Boroditsky demonstrates that a metaphor-framing effect does exist.' The replication is a close extension because the same paradigm was used but conducted in German with a different cultural population, and an additional factor (metaphor vs. simile) was added.

original_authors: Hampe, J.; Shaw, S.; Saiz, R.
original_title: Linkage of inflammatory bowel disease to human chromosome 6p
description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) susceptibility is linked to human chromosome 6p (IBD3 locus) based on multipoint LOD scores in affected sibling pair families
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'In the present study, we have replicated the 6p linkage in our IBD population containing 284 ASPs.' The nonparametric peak multipoint LOD score of 3.04 near D6S291 exceeded the proposed criteria for independent replication of significant linkage (LOD=1.5).

original_authors: Satsangi, J.; Parkes, M.; L.
original_title: Two stage genome-wide search in inflammatory bowel disease provides evidence for susceptibility loci on chromosomes 3, 7 and 12
description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) susceptibility is linked to chromosome 3p based on suggestive linkage in genome-wide scan of affected sibling pair families
explanation: The authors conducted an extension study in an expanded cohort of 284 IBD ASPs and found: 'Linkage was not detected in either the 3p or the 7q region.' The largest LOD score for 3p was only 1.25 for CD, and re-analysis of the original families also failed to support the earlier finding.

original_authors: Satsangi, J.; Parkes, M.; L.
original_title: Two stage genome-wide search in inflammatory bowel disease provides evidence for susceptibility loci on chromosomes 3, 7 and 12
description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) susceptibility is linked to chromosome 7q based on suggestive linkage in genome-wide scan of affected sibling pair families
explanation: The authors conducted an extension study in an expanded cohort of 284 IBD ASPs and found: 'Linkage was not detected in either the 3p or the 7q region.' The largest LOD score for 7q was only 1.26 for CD, and the paper notes that 'six genome scans and four replication studies have failed to detect linkage to chromosome 7,' suggesting the original finding may have been a false positive.

original_authors: Pankratz, N.; Nichols, W.; Uniacke, S.
original_title: Significant linkage of Parkinson disease to chromosome 2q36-37
description: Significant genetic linkage of Parkinson's disease to a 39.5 cM region on chromosome 2q36-37 (PARK11) under an autosomal dominant model of inheritance in families with strong family history of PD
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'performed a replication study' using the same markers, family selection criteria, and autosomal dominant model as Pankratz et al., but in a European population. The study found no significant linkage (highest LOD score 0.6, far below significance), concluding: 'our study did not provide evidence of a susceptibility locus for Parkinson's disease at 2q36-37 in our families.'

original_authors: Franchimont, D.; Vermeire, S.; El Housni, H.; Pierik, M.; Van Steen, K.; Gustot, T.
original_title: Deficient host-bacteria interactions in inflammatory bowel disease? The toll-like receptor (TLR)-4 Asp299gly polymorphism is associated with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis
description: The TLR4 Asp299Gly (TLR4 299Gly) polymorphism is associated with increased risk of Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis
explanation: The authors genotyped 1539 of their own IBD cases and combined with all published studies (4805 total cases), and explicitly state in the Discussion: 'we have found evidence to confirm the association of TLR4 299Gly with CD and IBD.' The pooled analysis (excluding original) shows OR=1.22 (95% CI: 1.06-1.40; P=0.002) for IBD, and all-studies pooled shows OR=1.26 (95% CI: 1.10-1.43; P=0.00017) for IBD and OR=1.33 (95% CI: 1.16-1.54; P=0.000035) for CD.

original_authors: Karban, A.; Okazaki, T.; Panhuysen, C.; Gallegos, T.; Potter, J.; Bailey-Wilson, J.
original_title: Functional annotation of a novel NFKB1 promoter polymorphism that increases risk for ulcerative colitis
description: The NFKB1 -94delATTG promoter polymorphism is associated with increased risk of ulcerative colitis
explanation: The authors' own samples showed no significant association (OR=0.99, 95% CI: 0.81-1.2), but pooled analysis with all published studies showed modest evidence (OR=1.12, 95% CI: 1.01-1.23; P=0.012) for UC only. The Discussion notes they 'provide more modest evidence that NFKB1 À94delATTG is a risk allele for UC,' indicating qualified rather than clear support.

original_authors: Chandy, K.; Fantino, E.; Wittekindt, O.; Kalman, K.; Tong, L.; Ho, T.
original_title: Isolation of a novel potassium channel gene hSKCa3 containing a polymorphic CAG repeat: a candidate for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder?
description: Longer CAG repeat alleles of the KCNN3 (hSKCa3) gene are significantly over-represented in schizophrenic patients compared to ethnically-matched controls in Caucasian populations from Europe and the USA
explanation: The authors explicitly tested whether the Chandy et al. (1998) finding of an association between longer KCNN3 CAG repeats and schizophrenia could be replicated in a Chinese population, using the same type of case-control genetic association design. They conclude: 'our data do not support that the second polymorphic CAG repeat of the KCNN3 gene may have an association with schizophrenia in our population' (p=0.664 and p=0.739 for their two statistical tests).

original_authors: Iwamoto, K.; Kakiuchi, C.; Bundo, M.; Ikeda, K.; Kato, T.
original_title: Molecular characterization of bipolar disorder by comparing gene expression profiles of postmortem brains of major mental disorders
description: LIM (PDLIM5) is significantly upregulated in the postmortem prefrontal cortex of patients with bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and major depression compared to healthy controls
explanation: The authors explicitly state they 'performed a replication study of altered expression levels of LIM' using an independent sample set (Stanley Array Collection), and in the Discussion confirm: 'upregulation of LIM in the postmortem frontal cortex of patients with bipolar disorder and schizophrenia was confirmed in a different sample set.' Significant upregulation was found for bipolar disorder (p<0.01) and schizophrenia (p<0.05).

original_authors: Melke, J.; Goubran Botros, H.; Chaste, P.; Betancur, C.; Nygren, G.; Anckarsater, H.
original_title: Abnormal melatonin synthesis in autism spectrum disorders
description: Variants in the ASMT gene (including splice site mutation IVS5+2T>C and promoter SNPs rs4446909 and rs5989681) are associated with increased susceptibility to autism spectrum disorders, with the major allele more frequent in ASD cases and linked to low ASMT transcript levels
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'In order to replicate the association results obtained by Melke et al., we also carried out a case-control study' and conclude that 'our data does not support a correlation between ASMT gene variants and increased susceptibility to ASDs.' No significant association was found for any SNPs or haplotypes across three independent European populations (Finnish, Italian, IMGSAC/UK) or in the combined sample.

original_authors: Deckert, J.; Nothen, M.; Franke, P.; Delmo, C.; Fritze, J.; Knapp, M.
original_title: Systematic mutation screening and association study of the A1 and A2a adenosine receptor genes in panic disorder suggest a contribution of the A2a gene to the development of disease
description: A silent coding polymorphism (1083C/T) in the adenosine 2A receptor gene (ADORA2A) is associated with panic disorder, with the T allele enriched in German panic disorder probands compared to controls
explanation: The authors find linkage evidence at the ADORA2A locus (max heterogeneity LOD = 2.98 at SNP-4) supporting the same chromosomal region, but their own association tests were not significant and the cosegregating allele in their haplotypes was C (not T as in Deckert et al.). The authors describe it as 'the first successful candidate gene replication study in panic disorder' based on the convergent linkage evidence, but the specific association reported by Deckert was not directly confirmed.

original_authors: Boland, M.; Shahn, Z.; Madigan, D.; Hripcsak, G.; Tatonetti, N.
original_title: Birth month affects lifetime disease risk: a phenome-wide method
original_journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association: JAMIA
description: Birth month is associated with lifetime cardiovascular disease risk, with risk peaking for those born in late winter/early spring, as identified via Season-Wide Association Study (SeaWAS) applied to electronic health records at Columbia University Medical Center
explanation: The authors applied the same SeaWAS method to an independent EHR dataset from Mount Sinai Hospital (MSH) in the same city (NYC). They found that 7 of 9 cardiovascular conditions identified at CUMC had significantly correlated seasonal birth-month risk patterns at MSH, with 4 reaching phenome-wide significance. The authors explicitly state: 'The replication findings bolster evidence for a seasonal birth month effect in CVD' and 'We confirm that CVD risk peaks for those born in the late winter/early spring.'

original_authors: Clements, C.; Castro, V.; Blumenthal, S.; Rosenfield, H.; Murphy, S.; Fava, M.
original_title: Prenatal antidepressant exposure is associated with risk for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder but not autism spectrum disorder in a large health system
description: Prenatal antidepressant exposure is not significantly associated with increased risk for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) after controlling for maternal psychopathology
explanation: The original study found no elevated ASD risk after controlling for maternal psychopathology. The replication confirmed this null finding (adjusted OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.50-1.54), with the authors concluding that 'prior reports of association between prenatal antidepressant exposure and neurodevelopmental disease are likely to represent a false-positive finding.'

original_authors: Clements, C.; Castro, V.; Blumenthal, S.; Rosenfield, H.; Murphy, S.; Fava, M.
original_title: Prenatal antidepressant exposure is associated with risk for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder but not autism spectrum disorder in a large health system
description: Prenatal antidepressant exposure is associated with elevated risk for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), persisting after adjustment for maternal psychiatric illness
explanation: The original study found elevated ADHD risk from prenatal antidepressant exposure that persisted despite adjustment for maternal psychopathology. The replication found no significant association (adjusted OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.53-1.69), with the authors explicitly acknowledging 'discordance between this result and our prior one with regard to ADHD.'

original_authors: Greenbaum, L.; Strous, R.; Kanyas, K.; Merbl, Y.; Horowitz, A.; Karni, O.
original_title: Association of the RGS2 gene with extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) induced by treatment with antipsychotic medication
description: Variants in the RGS2 gene, particularly the minor G allele of SNP rs4606 in the 3'-UTR, are associated with reduced susceptibility to antipsychotic-induced parkinsonism (AIP) in schizophrenia patients treated with antipsychotics
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as a 'cross-sectional replication study' and conclude that 'this replication study modestly supports the findings of our original report with regard to two RGS2 SNPs associated with AIP and identifies one of them (rs4606) as protective in all the samples studied.' The key finding — the protective effect of the rs4606 G allele against AIP — was replicated in a US sample of different ethnicity using a cross-sectional design, though the study used a different design and patient population (US African-American and Caucasian vs. Israeli Jewish) from the original prospective study.

original_authors: Mulder, H.; Franke, B.; Van Der-Beek Van Der Aart, A.; Arends, J.; Wilmink, F.; Scheffer, H.
original_title: The association between HTR2C gene polymorphisms and the metabolic syndrome in patients with schizophrenia
description: Carriership of the variant C-allele of the HTR2C rs1414334 polymorphism is associated with an increased prevalence of the metabolic syndrome in patients using antipsychotic drugs
explanation: The authors explicitly state this is a 'second replication' of their original 2007 findings and conclude: 'this study provides further evidence for the association between the HTR2C rs1414334 polymorphism and the metabolic syndrome, confirming previous findings.' The replication found a significant association (OR 3.73; 95% CI 1.29-10.79, P=0.015) in the same direction as the original (OR 4.09; 95% CI 1.41-11.89).

original_authors: Syu, A.; Ishiguro, H.; Inada, T.; Horiuchi, Y.; Tanaka, S.; Ishikawa, M.
original_title: Association of the HSPG2 gene with neuroleptic-induced tardive dyskinesia
description: The HSPG2 intronic SNP rs2445142 'G' risk allele is associated with increased susceptibility to tardive dyskinesia in schizophrenia patients treated with antipsychotics
explanation: The authors explicitly state they performed a 'replication study' of Syu et al. (2010) and found support for the HSPG2 rs2445142 association in two independent Caucasian samples. In the CATIE European sample (P=0.039) and the Jewish Israeli extreme phenotype sample (P=0.03), the same 'G' risk allele was confirmed: 'Support for association of the HSPG2 intronic SNP, rs2445142, with TD susceptibility was demonstrated.'

original_authors: Innocenti, F.; Kroetz, D.; Schuetz, E.; Dolan, M.; Ramirez, J.; Relling, M.
original_title: Comprehensive pharmacogenetic analysis of irinotecan neutropenia and pharmacokinetics
description: Genetic variants in five genes (UGT1A1, SLCO1B1, ABCC1, ABCC2, ABCB1) are associated with irinotecan-induced neutropenia (ANC nadir) and irinotecan pharmacokinetics in cancer patients treated with single-agent irinotecan
explanation: The study replicated 3 of 4 variants for ANC nadir (UGT1A1*28, UGT1A1*93, SLCO1B1*1b) and some pharmacokinetic associations, but ABCC1 IVS11-48C>T, SLCO1B1*5, ABCB1 IVS9-44A>G, and ABCC2 3972C>T failed to replicate. The authors state they 'validated the clinical effects of new germline genetic variants for neutropenia and irinotecan pharmacokinetics' but the overall picture is mixed, with several pre-specified variants failing to replicate.

original_authors: Kraft, S.; Ambrose, N.; Chon, H.
original_title: Temperament and environmental contributions to stuttering severity in children: The role of effortful control
description: Effortful control (EC) is the sole significant predictor of stuttering severity in children who stutter, independent of home environment and significant life events
explanation: The Discussion explicitly states 'findings were robustly consistent with those reported by [Kraft et al. 2014],' with EC remaining the sole significant predictor of both parent-reported and clinician-reported stuttering severity in the Australian cohort. The replication used the same questionnaires and analytical approach but with a different (larger, Australian) population.

original_authors: Eynon, N.; Oliveira, J.; Meckel, Y.; Sagiv, M.; Yamin, C.; Sagiv, M.; Amir, R.; Duarte, J.
original_title: The guanine nucleotide binding protein beta polypeptide 3 gene C825T polymorphism is associated with elite endurance athletes
description: The TT genotype of the GNB3 C825T polymorphism is associated with elite endurance athletic status, with Israeli elite endurance athletes showing a higher frequency of the TT genotype compared to sprinters
explanation: The authors explicitly state that 'the previous association reported by Eynon et al. [4] between the GNB3 TT genotype and elite endurance athletic status...was not corroborated here in a larger cohort.' The summary concludes: 'we did not find an association between the GNB3 C825T polymorphism and elite athletic status.' All comparisons showed P > 0.1, and the OR for endurance vs. controls was 0.841 (95% CI: 0.638–1.110).

original_authors: Salis, C.
original_title: Short-term memory treatment: patterns of learning and generalisation to sentence comprehension in a person with aphasia
description: Short-term memory treatment using a matching listening span task improves spoken sentence comprehension in a person with aphasia
explanation: The authors explicitly state that 'None of the persons in the current replication improved in sentence comprehension,' and no statistically significant changes were found on any sentence comprehension outcome measures using McNemar chi-square tests.

original_authors: Hodgson, T.; Magrabi, F.; Coiera, E.
original_title: Efficiency and safety of speech recognition for documentation in the electronic health record
original_journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
description: Using speech recognition (SR) for clinical documentation tasks in an electronic health record (EHR) is associated with significantly more data entry errors and longer documentation times compared to keyboard and mouse (KBM) input
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'The results of this study largely replicate those reported in the original experiment. The use of SR while performing clinical documentation tasks within an EHR system was associated with decreased time efficiencies and increased data entry errors.' The Conclusion further confirms: 'The results of the replication study provide strong supporting evidence that SR-assisted clinical documentation in an EHR is both slower and produces more documentation errors than KBM alone.'

original_authors: Philipp, V.; Beck, R.; Scherhag, M.; Glocke, R.; Schmidt
original_title: Biological and psychopathological prediction of response to doxepine in depressive outpatients
description: Psychopathological factors (including Newcastle Scale criteria, endogenous/nonendogenous classification, number of prior episodes, and early improvement) predict doxepine response in depressed outpatients treated in a psychiatric private practice setting
explanation: The replication confirmed some hypotheses from the original study (70% response rate achieved at 74%, endogenous classification not predictive, early 2-week improvement predicts remission, and 'no deviating personality' predicts response) but failed to confirm others (three of four Newcastle criteria: anxiety, weight loss, blaming others; and number of prior depressive episodes). The authors explicitly note both confirmed and unconfirmed findings, indicating a mixed/partial replication.

original_authors: Buijsen, E.
original_title: Self portrait with gorget Portrait of Rembrandt with a gorget
original_journal: Self portrait with gorget Portrait of Rembrandt with a gorget
description: Dendrochronological analysis by Klein in the 1990s dated the wood panels of two portraits of Rembrandt (at the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Nuremberg, and the Mauritshuis, The Hague) to specific outermost ring dates, estimated felling dates, and concluded the GNM panel originated from the same tree as a Rijksmuseum panel
explanation: The reproduction (using Klein's original data and reference chronologies) confirmed the original dating results for both portraits. The authors state: 'the reproduction and replication of the dendrochronological research of the panels of two portraits of a young Rembrandt carried out in the 1990s have confirmed the dates for the wood reported by Klein in the 1990s.' The reproduction also confirmed the same-tree match between the GNM and Rijksmuseum panels, though it identified measurement errors in Klein's original data.

original_authors: Buijsen, E.
original_title: Self portrait with gorget Portrait of Rembrandt with a gorget
original_journal: Self portrait with gorget Portrait of Rembrandt with a gorget
description: Dendrochronological analysis by Klein in the 1990s dated the wood panels of two portraits of Rembrandt (at the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Nuremberg, and the Mauritshuis, The Hague) to specific outermost ring dates, estimated felling dates, and concluded the GNM panel originated from the same tree as a Rijksmuseum panel
explanation: The conceptual replication using state-of-the-art methods (digital photography, CooRecorder software, modern reference chronologies) confirmed all of Klein's main findings. The authors explicitly state both approaches 'confirmed the original results, including the southern Baltic provenance of the wood and a same-tree match between the Nuremberg and Rijksmuseum panels.' The new measurements produced an 'outstanding match' with the RM panel, further supporting that both panels originate from the same tree.

original_authors: Walker, M.; Brakefield, T.; Hobson, J.; Stickgold, R.
original_title: Dissociable stages of human memory consolidation and reconsolidation
description: Postretrieval new learning (interference) causes a substantial decline (~57%) in accuracy of a previously learned motor sequence, indicating reconsolidation-mediated memory updating (group 7 of original study)
explanation: In four direct replication attempts (n=64), the authors 'did not observe the critical impairment effect that has previously been taken to indicate disruption of an existing motor memory trace.' Mean reconsolidation score declined by <1% for accuracy across experiments, compared to ~57% in the original, and Bayesian analysis consistently favored the null hypothesis over the reconsolidation hypothesis.

original_authors: Walker, M.; Brakefield, T.; Hobson, J.; Stickgold, R.
original_title: Dissociable stages of human memory consolidation and reconsolidation
description: Postretrieval new learning (interference) causes a substantial decline (~57%) in accuracy of a previously learned motor sequence, indicating reconsolidation-mediated memory updating (group 7 of original study)
explanation: Three conceptual replications (n=48) using declarative recall of phone-number and password-like sequences also failed to find reconsolidation-contingent impairment. Performance decrements occurred equally in the presence and absence of a memory retrieval reminder, and retrieval actually led to numerically higher performance than the no-retrieval control group — the opposite of what reconsolidation theory predicts.

original_authors: Tversky, A.; Kahneman, D.
original_title: The framing of decisions and the psychology of choice
description: Framing identical choice outcomes as potential losses (vs. gains) causes people to become more risk-seeking (the 'Asian Disease' gain-loss framing effect)
explanation: The authors explicitly state in their discussion that they 'found the same gain-loss framing effect for two information topics (customs and languages) that has been observed for other outcomes, such as human lives,' directly referencing the Tversky & Kahneman Asian Disease paradigm. Study 3 is itself labeled as a 'conceptual replication of the classic Asian Disease gain-loss pattern' using facts instead of human lives.

original_authors: Cohn, A.; Maréchal, M.; Tannenbaum, D.; Zünd, C.
original_title: Civic honesty around the globe
description: Wallets containing money have a significantly higher email response rate than wallets without money when dropped at urban institutions across 40 countries
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'this study successfully reproduced that study's main finding: The email response rate was significantly higher in the "money" condition than in the "no money" condition.' The replication found email response rates of 32.7% (money) vs. 22.2% (no money), P = 0.009, matching the direction and significance of Cohn et al.'s original result.

original_authors: Houtepen, L.; Vinkers, C.; Carrillo-Roa, T.; Hiemstra, M.; Van Lier, P.; Meeus, W.; Boks, M.
original_title: Genome-wide DNA methylation levels and altered cortisol stress reactivity following childhood trauma in humans
description: KITLG gene DNA methylation is negatively associated with cortisol stress reactivity (increased methylation corresponds to lower cortisol levels under stress)
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'Our study thus provides the first independent replication of findings published in the younger cohort', finding a significant negative association between CpG 2.3 KITLG DNA methylation and cortisol under stress conditions (both morning cortisol and AUC), though the significant CpG site differed from the original (CpG 2.3 vs. CpG 1) and the association did not survive stringent multiple testing correction.

original_authors: Houtepen, L.; Vinkers, C.; Carrillo-Roa, T.; Hiemstra, M.; Van Lier, P.; Meeus, W.; Boks, M.
original_title: Genome-wide DNA methylation levels and altered cortisol stress reactivity following childhood trauma in humans
description: Childhood trauma (retrospective self-report) is positively associated with KITLG DNA methylation in adults
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'we were not able to replicate the correlation between childhood trauma and KITLG methylation', with no significant associations found between childhood adversity measures (parental death, physical/sexual abuse, or number of adverse events) and KITLG DNA methylation at any of the seven CpG units.

original_authors: Hirsch, O.; Christiansen, H.
original_title: Faking ADHD? symptom validity testing and its relation to self-reported, observer-reported symptoms, and neuropsychological measures of attention in adults with ADHD
description: Substantial base rates of noncredible symptom report and cognitive performance exist in adults undergoing clinical evaluation for ADHD, and measures of symptom validity (SVT) and performance validity (PVT) are only marginally and non-significantly related to each other
explanation: The SVT (CII) failure rate was closely replicated (35.7% vs. 36.6%) and the poor SVT-PVT association was confirmed, but the ASTM PVT failure rate was not stable (32.1% original vs. 49.3% replication). The authors note that 'unstable ASTM failure rates and sensitivity to changes in design and procedure may question its reliability,' reflecting mixed confirmation of the original findings.

original_authors: Saffran, J.; Hauser, M.; Seibel, R.; Kapfhamer, J.; Tsao, F.; Cushman, F.
original_title: Grammatical pattern learning by human infants and cotton-top tamarin monkeys
description: Predictive dependencies between words in an artificial grammar facilitate phrase structure learning in 12-month-old infants, such that infants exposed to grammars with predictive dependencies (but not those without) successfully discriminate familiar from novel grammar-inconsistent test strings
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as 'a conceptual replication of Saffran et al. (2008, Exp. 1)' and conclude: 'As previously observed with linguistic materials, 12-month-old infants showed better learning when predictive dependencies characterized nonlinguistic phrase structure,' successfully replicating the original pattern using nonlinguistic auditory materials (computer alert sounds) instead of nonsense words.

original_authors: Yu, L.; Chibnik, L.; Srivastava, G.
original_title: Association of brain DNA methylation in SORL1, ABCA7, HLA-DRB5, SLC24A4, and BIN1 with pathological diagnosis of Alzheimer disease
description: BIN1 gene-wide DNA methylation differences in post-mortem brain (cortical) cells are associated with Alzheimer's disease pathological diagnosis
explanation: The replication found no significant association between BIN1 gene-wide DNA methylation and dementia or AD in leukocytes (p = 0.07 for dementia, p = 0.05 for AD), failing to replicate the original brain-based finding. The authors note that BIN1 was 'close to significance' but did not reach the p < 0.05 threshold.

original_authors: Yu, L.; Chibnik, L.; Srivastava, G.
original_title: Association of brain DNA methylation in SORL1, ABCA7, HLA-DRB5, SLC24A4, and BIN1 with pathological diagnosis of Alzheimer disease
description: HLA-DRB5 gene-wide DNA methylation differences in post-mortem brain (cortical) cells are associated with Alzheimer's disease pathological diagnosis
explanation: HLA-DRB5 showed significant association with dementia in leukocytes (p = 0.02) but co-twin control analyses and further investigation revealed the result was largely driven by a single CpG site, and the association was not significant for AD in co-twin control analyses. The authors conclude that 'familial confounding appears to drive part of the associations' and the co-twin control dementia result 'is thus likely driven by a single spurious finding.'

original_authors: Yu, L.; Chibnik, L.; Srivastava, G.
original_title: Association of brain DNA methylation in SORL1, ABCA7, HLA-DRB5, SLC24A4, and BIN1 with pathological diagnosis of Alzheimer disease
description: SORL1 gene-wide DNA methylation differences in post-mortem brain (cortical) cells are associated with Alzheimer's disease pathological diagnosis
explanation: No significant association was found between SORL1 gene-wide DNA methylation and dementia or AD in leukocytes (p = 0.06 for dementia, p = 0.10 for AD), failing to replicate the original brain-based finding. The authors note this is 'in line with previous findings in blood' that also failed to find SORL1 associations.

original_authors: Yu, L.; Chibnik, L.; Srivastava, G.
original_title: Association of brain DNA methylation in SORL1, ABCA7, HLA-DRB5, SLC24A4, and BIN1 with pathological diagnosis of Alzheimer disease
description: SLC24A4 gene-wide DNA methylation differences in post-mortem brain (cortical) cells are associated with Alzheimer's disease pathological diagnosis
explanation: SLC24A4 showed significant association with dementia in leukocytes (p = 0.01) but was weakened in co-twin control analyses (p = 0.17), indicating the association is partly explained by familial confounding. The authors state 'the association between DNA methylation of SLC24A4 and dementia or AD risk was weakened in co-twin control analyses, indicating that the association is partly, but not fully, driven by genetic or other familial confounding.'

original_authors: Yu, L.; Chibnik, L.; Srivastava, G.
original_title: Association of brain DNA methylation in SORL1, ABCA7, HLA-DRB5, SLC24A4, and BIN1 with pathological diagnosis of Alzheimer disease
description: ABCA7 gene-wide DNA methylation differences in post-mortem brain (cortical) cells are associated with Alzheimer's disease pathological diagnosis
explanation: No significant association was found between ABCA7 gene-wide DNA methylation and dementia or AD in leukocytes (p = 0.24 for dementia, p = 0.23 for AD), clearly failing to replicate the original brain-based finding. The authors note this is 'in line with previous findings in blood.'

original_authors: Wichert S; Wolf O; Schwabe L
original_title: Changing memories after reactivation: A one-time opportunity?
description: Reactivation of consolidated episodic memories followed by new learning impairs memory, whereas new learning alone or reactivation alone does not produce memory impairment
explanation: The authors explicitly titled the paper 'a failed replication study' and conclude in the Discussion: 'we did not find that the crucial expected difference between Re+NL and NL alone was substantially supported by the data, for any of our dependent measures.' The critical comparison between reactivation+new learning and new learning alone — the key test of reconsolidation — showed only anecdotal Bayesian evidence (BF10 = 1.99 for recognition accuracy), far below the threshold for substantial support.

original_authors: Lommen, M.; Engelhard, I.; Sijbrandij, M.; Van Den Hout, M.; Hermans, D.
original_title: Pre-trauma individual differences in extinction learning predict posttraumatic stress
description: Reduced pre-trauma extinction learning (measured via US-expectancy ratings) predicts greater PTSD symptom severity after deployment, even when controlling for baseline PTSD symptoms, neuroticism, and stressor severity
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'The finding of [16] that reduced extinction learning predicted subsequent PTSD symptoms, even after controlling for existing PTSD symptoms, neuroticism and stressor severity, was not replicated in the present study.' Extinction learning was not a significant predictor of PTSD symptom severity in Model 1 (β = .05, F < 1), and the paper concludes that 'the findings of Lommen and colleagues (2013) were not replicated in the current sample.'

original_authors: Jones, G.; Proto, D.; Musso, M.; Barker, A.; Gouvier, W.
original_title: Using the NAART to estimate WRAT-4 reading grade level in a predominantly African American sample
description: NAART error scores and WRAT4 Word Reading subtest raw scores are significantly correlated, and a regression equation derived from NAART error scores can accurately predict reading grade level classification
explanation: The correlation was successfully replicated (r = -.91 vs original r = -.87), but results were mixed for the regression equation: it accurately classified fifth-grade reading level (Cohen's Kappa = .78) but added no predictive value beyond chance for fourth-grade reading level (Cohen's Kappa = .00), and the WRAT4 score distributions differed significantly between samples (Z = 3.804, p < .001). The authors conclude the equation 'can be applied to the current sample to accurately predict reading classification' but acknowledge the mixed pattern of results.

original_authors: Rabbitt, P.
original_title: Channel-capacity, intelligibility and immediate memory
original_journal: The Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology
description: Listening to speech in noise in the second half of a digit list impairs recall for items presented earlier in the list, even when those earlier items were not themselves presented in noise
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'The results robustly support Rabbitt's main finding: the presence of noise disrupts recall of previously heard information.' The replication effect size (Cohen's d = 0.19) was identical to that reported in the original study.

original_authors: Funayama, M.; Hasegawa, K.; Kowa, H.; Saito, M.; Tsuji, S.; Obata, F.
original_title: A new locus for Parkinson's disease (PARK8) maps to chromosome 12p11.2-q13.1
description: The PARK8 locus on chromosome 12 is linked to autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease, as originally identified in a large Japanese family with levodopa-responsive parkinsonism
explanation: The authors explicitly call this a 'replication study' and report a maximum multipoint LOD score of 2.01 (P=.0047), concluding: 'Our data provide evidence that the PARK8 locus is responsible for the disease in a subset of families of white ancestry with autosomal dominant parkinsonism, suggesting that it could be a more common locus.' The study tests the same genetic locus in a different (white/European) population, confirming linkage.

original_authors: Hanna, G.; Veenstra-Vanderweele, J.; Cox, N.; Boehnke, M.; Himle, J.; Curtis, G.; Leventhal, B.; Cook, E.
original_title: Genome-wide linkage analysis of families with obsessive-compulsive disorder ascertained through pediatric probands
description: Genome-wide linkage scan identified a candidate susceptibility region for OCD on chromosome 9p24 at marker D9S288, achieving suggestive linkage significance
explanation: The authors explicitly state they performed 'an attempt to replicate this finding' and conclude that 'this initial 9p24 replication study provides promising additional evidence for an OCD susceptibility gene in this region.' The replication found linkage peaks (HLOD=2.26, NPL=2.52, p=.006) within 0.5 cM of the original signal at D9S288, which the authors describe as 'striking' and confirmatory.

original_authors: Chen, Q.; He, G.; Wang, X.; Chen, Q.; Liu, X.; Gu, Z.; Liu, J.; Li, K.; Wang, S.; Zhu, S.; Feng, G.; He, L.
original_title: Positive association between synapsin II and schizophrenia
description: Synapsin II gene variants (particularly SNP rs795009 and a four-marker haplotype) are positively associated with schizophrenia susceptibility in Han Chinese, as measured by allele-frequency differences in a case-control study
explanation: The authors explicitly describe the present study as a 'replication study' of their prior case-control work (Chen et al. 2004), using a fundamentally different methodology (family-based transmission/disequilibrium test rather than case-control allele frequency comparison). The Discussion concludes: 'our results provide further support for our previous study [1] that showed that synapsin II may be an important gene in the predisposition to schizophrenia,' with five of six markers showing significant transmission distortion.
